stories.headline: Dawn Staley, South Carolina hosting Thanksgiving tournament to benefit HBCUs
stories.summary: Dawn Staley's South Carolina Gamecocks will host the PowHER Player Classic at Colonial Life Arena in Columbia on November 28-29, a four-team tournament with three HBCUs, North Carolina Central, Alabama A&M and Tennessee State, HBCU News reports. Beyond the games, the weekend includes a Thanksgiving community service project, an NIL marketplace and a Culture Night dinner, with Staley framing the event as a vehicle for access and opportunity for HBCU players rather than a standard paycheck game.

stories.headline: Drax Foundation invests in Mississippi HBCUs to connect students to educational opportunities
stories.summary: Four Mississippi HBCUs, Alcorn State, Jackson State, Mississippi Valley State and Tougaloo College, will share $100,000 from the Drax Foundation to support student advancement and programming, renewable energy company Drax announced on November 27. Mississippi Valley State's $25,000 will fund its Skill Readiness and Retention Project for the freshman-to-sophomore transition, while Alcorn State's $25,000 establishes the Drax Foundation Scholars Program, taking Drax's total investment at Alcorn to $75,000.

stories.headline: Three HBCU football stars named finalists for Walter Payton Award
stories.summary: Three HBCU standouts, Alcorn State quarterback Jaylon Tolbert, South Carolina State quarterback Keely Watson and Southern running back Trey Holly, are among the 30 finalists for the 2026 Walter Payton Award, Stats Perform announced, HBCU News reports. Tolbert threw for 3,648 yards and an FCS-best 38 touchdowns among finalist quarterbacks, Watson threw 20 touchdowns against just three interceptions for MEAC champion South Carolina State, and Holly rushed for 1,393 yards and 14 touchdowns; the award honours former Jackson State great Walter Payton.

stories.headline: Alabama State Dominates Tuskegee 45-0 in 102nd Turkey Day Classic
stories.summary: Alabama State shut out Tuskegee 45-0 in the 102nd Turkey Day Classic at ASU Stadium in Montgomery on Thanksgiving Day, in front of 16,867 fans, HBCU News reports. The Hornets outgained the Golden Tigers 428-152, led 28-0 at halftime behind quarterback Aaron Frye, and got a fumble-return touchdown from Mitchell Robinson Jr., who also made 10 tackles; Alabama State finished 7-5 in Eddie Robinson Jr.'s fifth season, while Tuskegee closed at 5-6.

stories.headline: Historic Macy’s Parade Postponement Bumps Marquee HBCU Classic Off NBC
stories.summary: The first weather postponement of the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has bumped the 53rd Bayou Classic between Grambling State and Southern off NBC's main network, HBCU News reports. The game will still air live nationwide on NBCSN and stream on Peacock on Saturday, November 28, with kickoff at 1 p.m. CT at the Caesars Superdome in New Orleans and Louisiana NBC affiliates carrying it locally; Southern, 6-5 under first-year coach Marshall Faulk, seeks a fifth straight Bayou Classic win.

stories.headline: Bears, Eagles and Bills win as NFL serves up Thanksgiving thrillers
stories.summary: All three NFL Thanksgiving games were decided in the final seconds, AFP reports via SportBeep. Caleb Williams hit Rome Odunze with three seconds left as Chicago beat Detroit 39-35 to take the NFC North lead despite Jahmyr Gibbs rushing for 205 yards and three touchdowns for the Lions; Joe Milton threw for 331 yards as Philadelphia erased a 21-point deficit to beat Dallas 39-38 on a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left; and Tyler Bass kicked a 57-yarder as time expired in Buffalo's 13-10 win over Patrick Mahomes and Kansas City.

stories.headline: Data park project draws $50m investor push from Nigeria, Togo
stories.summary: Nigeria and Togo are seeking private investors to finance the first phase of a joint twin data park project estimated at $30 million to $50 million, TechCabal reports. The two governments signed a memorandum of understanding for one facility in each country, announced by Nigeria's Bosun Tijani and Togo's Cina Lawson in Lagos on November 26; the Nigerian site would sit beside the Egbin Power Plant, both governments would hold minority stakes, and the ministers want elements in place by the second quarter of 2027.

stories.headline: NHI clears major legal hurdle in Constitutional Court
stories.summary: South Africa's Constitutional Court has dismissed two challenges to the National Health Insurance Act's parliamentary process, removing a major legal obstacle to the government's planned health care overhaul, Moneyweb reports, citing Bloomberg. The court unanimously dismissed the Board of Healthcare Funders' case and, by 6-5, the Western Cape government's challenge over public participation; broader challenges to the NHI and questions over its funding and implementation remain unresolved, and the 2024 law has not yet come into operation.

stories.headline: Obado to Appeal 25-Year Jail Term, Lawyers Cite Impact on Sharon Otieno’s Family
stories.summary: Former Migori Governor Okoth Obado's lawyers say they will appeal his 25-year prison sentence for the murder of Rongo University student Sharon Otieno, calling the punishment unfair and disproportionate, Capital FM reports from Nairobi. Obado and his former personal assistant Michael Juma Oyamo each received 25 years on November 27, while former county clerk Caspal Ojwang Obiero received 18 years; the court described Obado as the principal architect of the 2018 killing of Otieno, who was 26 and seven months pregnant.

stories.headline: Wu-Tang Clan Bring Da Ruckus for NFL Thanksgiving Day Halftime Show
stories.summary: Wu-Tang Clan headlined the Detroit Lions' Thanksgiving halftime show against the Chicago Bears, performing classics including 'Triumph,' 'Protect Ya Neck,' 'C.R.E.A.M.' and 'Method Man' with Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer Chad Smith on drums and ODB's son Young Dirty Bastard trading verses, Consequence reports. The booking, curated by Eminem and Paul Rosenberg under their multi-year partnership with the Lions, came less than two weeks after the Staten Island group's induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

stories.headline: Zuku wins back customers, but losses continue under Axian
stories.summary: Kenyan home internet provider Zuku is winning back subscribers with cheaper packages and faster speeds, but its parent Wananchi Group is still losing money a year after Axian Telecom acquired it, TechCabal reports. Wananchi posted a $2 million third-quarter loss on revenue of $11.5 million and has accumulated $8.1 million in losses since January, even as Zuku's fixed-internet subscriptions grew 10.4 percent in the first half of 2026 after it doubled speeds and cut prices.

stories.headline: Kenya drops FlexPay criminal case in $240,000 Naivas dispute
stories.summary: Kenyan prosecutors have dropped criminal charges against four FlexPay executives over KES 31.2 million ($240,000) claimed by supermarket chain Naivas, finding the dispute civil in nature and advising Naivas to pursue the money in civil court, TechCabal reports. The decision ends months of investigation after the collapse of a five-year partnership through which the fintech processed more than KES 3 billion in customer transactions for Kenya's largest supermarket chain; neither ruling settled the companies' competing financial claims.

stories.headline: Tinubu Vows To Rescue 78 Kidnapped Borno Schoolchildren
stories.summary: President Bola Tinubu has pledged at an APC rally in Maiduguri to rescue the 78 schoolchildren abducted by insurgents in Askira-Uba, Borno State, six months ago, S24 Television reports, sourcing Daily Trust. Forty-two children were taken from Mussa on May 15 and 36 from Lassa on June 29; parents, who have protested for months, told reporters they are tired of promises without visible rescue efforts, while Tinubu praised the armed forces and urged insurgents to surrender.

stories.headline: Orlando Pirates begin Champions League group stage against 22-time Tanzanian champions Simba
stories.summary: Orlando Pirates open their 2026/27 CAF Champions League group-stage campaign against Simba SC in Dar es Salaam on Sunday, in front of a potential 60,000 crowd at Benjamin Mkapa Stadium, African Football reports. Pirates, who lead South Africa's Betway Premiership with 28 points from 10 matches and reached the group stage without conceding in qualifying, are in Group C with Simba, Morocco's RS Berkane and Cameroon's Colombe Sportive; VAR will be used in the group stage.

stories.headline: NPP says gifted-pupil exemption was added ‘after public outcry’ over BECE ban
stories.summary: Ghana's opposition NPP says the exemption for exceptionally gifted pupils in the government's two-year ban on early BECE candidates was added only after public outcry, GhanaGuardian reports. Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu announced on November 23 that JHS 1 and JHS 2 pupils who sit the Basic Education Certificate Examination early would be barred for two years; NPP education committee co-chair Dr Prince Hamid Armah, speaking on Joy FM on November 26, called the gifted-pupil provision an afterthought and urged withdrawal of the ban.

stories.headline: NBA roundup: LeBron James' triple-double helps 76ers end Heat's win streak
stories.summary: LeBron James recorded his first triple-double as a Philadelphia 76er, with 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds, as the 76ers beat the visiting Miami Heat 111-104 on Wednesday to snap Miami's seven-game winning streak, Reuters reports. Tyrese Maxey added 30 points for Philadelphia while Giannis Antetokounmpo had 32 points and 14 rebounds for Miami; elsewhere in NBA Cup play, the Knicks beat the Cavaliers 121-102 for a sixth straight win, the Grizzlies beat the Clippers 115-97, and the Warriors beat the Kings 129-110 behind De'Anthony Melton's 24 points, all from three-point range.

stories.headline: Kenya breached constitution by allowing US-backed Ebola quarantine site, court says
stories.summary: A Kenyan High Court ruled on Thursday that the government breached parts of the constitution by allowing construction of a U.S.-backed Ebola quarantine facility at Laikipia Air Base without public participation, Reuters reports. Judge Patricia Nyaundi said residents of Laikipia County had been denied a meaningful opportunity to know about or question the 50-bed facility, and the court ordered further work stopped until the government discloses details of its agreement with the United States; the project had sparked protests in which two young people died, and Kenya has reported no new Ebola case since October 19.

stories.headline: Black Promoters Collective Plans July 4th Takeover in New Orleans
stories.summary: Black Promoters Collective, described as the largest Black-owned live entertainment company in the country and 100 percent Black-owned, is planning a Fourth of July weekend takeover in New Orleans, Baller Alert reports exclusively. The collective, behind the Brandy and Monica co-headlining tour and ranked No. 10 on Billboard's Midyear 2026 Top Promoters chart, is aiming to make its event the must-attend festival of the year on the weekend long held by the Essence Festival, whose multiyear contract with the city expired in September.

stories.headline: AI/ML Engineer Dr. Syreeta Rios Created An AI-Powered Career And Project Platform For Black And Brown Women
stories.summary: AI and machine learning engineer Dr. Syreeta Rios has created Ascend AI, an AI-powered career and project management platform designed to help Black and brown women navigate corporate environments, AfroTech reports. Launched in June and demoed at the 2026 AFROTECH Conference, Ascend offers an AI advisor for workplace decisions and performance reviews, project and promotion tracking, quarterly career goals and a journal, drawing its dataset from Black-identified research and books by Black women leaders; membership is $19 a month, with an Employee Resource Group plan at $2,500 a year.

stories.headline: Delaware State University Names Dr. Yah Williams Founding Director of the Center for Economic Mobility
stories.summary: Delaware State University has appointed Dr. Yahshikiah 'Yah' Williams as founding director of its new Center for Economic Mobility, the university-wide centre established this fall to put every student on a path to a good job, the university announced on November 24. Williams, currently assistant dean in the College of Business, where she built the executive mentoring program and the DEEP Day career event, takes up the role on November 30; the centre runs on the Braven platform with a sophomore-year career accelerator for all students, and 71 percent of its most recent Braven Fellows come from low-income households.

stories.headline: Drake State Receives $20,000 Grant For Workforce Development Initiatives
stories.summary: Drake State Community and Technical College in Huntsville, Alabama, has been awarded a $20,000 grant from the Alabama HBCU Consortium to support workforce development initiatives that prepare students for high-demand careers, HBCU News reports. The grant, awarded at an MOU signing on campus, will help the historically Black college expand workforce training, industry-aligned credentials and career preparation programs connecting students with employers across North Alabama.

stories.headline: Bison Trio Named to the 2026-27 HBCU All-Stars Watch List
stories.summary: Three Howard University guards, Alex Cotton, Cam Gillus and Ose Okojie, have been named to the sixth annual HBCU All-Stars Watch List, HBCU All-Stars LLC announced on November 25. The watch list recognises the nation's top HBCU student-athletes from the MEAC, SWAC, CIAA and SIAC plus Hampton, North Carolina A&T and Tennessee State; the 2027 HBCU All-Star Game, showcasing 24 players, will be held on March 28, 2027 at the McCamish Pavilion in Atlanta.

stories.headline: HBCU Football Transfer Portal: Announcements and Rumors, November 2026
stories.summary: More than 20 HBCU football players across the MEAC, SWAC, CIAA and SIAC had announced plans to enter the NCAA transfer portal as of November 25, the HBCU Legends tracker reported by Sports Illustrated finds, as the 2026 season winds down. The group includes all-conference Morgan State offensive tackle Kelton Sparks, former FCS Freshman All-American Delaware State quarterback Marqui Adams and Texas Southern running back Athean Renfro Jr.; the single Division I transfer window runs January 4-13, 2027, with announcements so far reflecting intentions rather than official entries.

stories.headline: Amini wants to turn Africa's paper archives into data for AI
stories.summary: Amini, a startup building sovereign AI infrastructure for governments in the Global South, has released Soma-1X Lite, an open-weight AI model that converts paper records into machine-readable data, TechCabal reports. The two-billion-parameter model processes about 15,000 pages an hour and recorded the lowest character error rate, 2.9 percent, among five models tested on 435 pages across ten African languages including Yoruba, Hausa, Swahili and Wolof; Amini, founded in 2022 by former Nvidia executive Kate Kallot, is working with Botswana's Ministry of Minerals and Energy to digitise decades of geological records, and has published the model's weights and evaluation code on Hugging Face.

stories.headline: Four SA students build fintech to fix bursary pay problems
stories.summary: Four South African university students, Brian Mbana, Aaron Matsemela, Cliff Kaela and Simanye Sobekwa, are building CampusFit, a fintech platform to help students access, manage and track their bursary allowances without the delays that leave many stranded, TechCabal reports. Born at a hackathon in East London, CampusFit plans instant peer-to-peer transfers, budgeting tools and a single dashboard linking a student's bank accounts; the founders have built a minimum viable product, expect to onboard students in the coming months, and are in the Genesis Block incubation cohort backed by FNB and the University of Cape Town Financial Innovation Hub.

stories.headline: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Dies At 79
stories.summary: Veteran Nigerian actor and retired broadcaster Chief Pete Edochie has died at 79, his family announced; he died at 12:30 a.m. on Wednesday, November 25, in Enugu after a protracted battle with prostate cancer, Voice of Nigeria reports. Edochie, who began in broadcasting in 1967, rose to prominence as Okonkwo in the 1987 Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe's Things Fall Apart and became one of Nollywood's most commanding screen figures; he held the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger and is survived by his wife Josephine, children, siblings and other relations.

stories.headline: Hakimi, Mané, Brahim Diaz, Saibari and Pape Gueye as named in final five for CAF Men's Player of the Year 2026
stories.summary: CAF has unveiled the five finalists for the CAF Men's Player of the Year 2026 award: reigning holder Achraf Hakimi, Brahim Diaz and Ismael Saibari of Morocco, and Sadio Mané and Pape Gueye of Senegal, CAF announced. The shortlist, cut from ten nominees, reflects Senegal's triumph at AFCON Morocco 2025, where Mané was named Best Player and Gueye scored the extra-time winner in the final, and Morocco's run to the World Cup quarter-finals; the winner will be crowned at the CAF Awards in Lagos, Nigeria, on December 2.

stories.headline: Banks get nod to sell $1m cash to BDCs as CBN targets gap in currency rate
stories.summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria has authorised banks to sell up to $1 million in cash to bureau de change operators, raising the supply of physical dollars in the retail foreign exchange market, BusinessDay reports. The policy, effective Wednesday, November 25, lets operators take their full allocation in cash, replacing an arrangement that capped cash withdrawals at 25 percent of the approved limit; the central bank notified lenders by email and will supply additional dollar notes where needed, a day after Governor Olayemi Cardoso attributed recent pressure on the naira to seasonal year-end demand.

stories.headline: Senegal parliament adopts resolution opposing president's decision to implement budget
stories.summary: Senegal's National Assembly on Wednesday adopted a resolution, by 128 votes to 9, denouncing President Bassirou Diomaye Faye's decision to implement a revised 2026 budget by decree after lawmakers rejected it, Reuters reports. The standoff, between Faye and his former prime minister Ousmane Sonko, whose Pastef party controls the Assembly, threatens a new $2.2 billion IMF support programme that underpins Senegal's plan to rework its debt burden; Pastef lawmakers argued the government had not provided sufficient transparency over public finances and the debt assumptions behind the revised budget.

stories.headline: Flat October salaries reflect a tough year
stories.summary: South African take-home pay stayed flat in October 2026, with the PayInc Net Salary Index, tracking about 2.1 million salary earners, unchanged at R21,680 and up only 1.8 percent on a year ago, IT-Online reports. In real terms the index fell to R20,094, 2.9 percent lower than a year ago, as headline inflation spiked to 5.2 percent on fuel price increases; economist Elize Kruger said average net salaries are down 2.3 percent in real terms year to date, likely the worst year since 2023, though easing fuel prices could restore some purchasing power in 2027.

stories.headline: Celtics build 34-point lead then hold off Wizards
stories.summary: Jayson Tatum scored 41 points with six rebounds and eight assists as Boston ended a four-game losing streak by beating Washington 131-116 in an NBA Cup game on Tuesday, Reuters reports. Boston built a 34-point first-half lead and led 80-49 at halftime before Washington cut the margin to five in the fourth quarter; Paul George added 28 points, Anthony Davis had 33 points and 13 rebounds for the Wizards, and Boston stayed unbeaten at 3-0 in Eastern Group C.

stories.headline: Nigeria seizes more than $200 million of meth, arrests five Mexicans
stories.summary: Nigeria's anti-drug agency said on Wednesday it had seized methamphetamine valued at $227 million and arrested five Mexican nationals in the southeastern state of Enugu, Reuters reports. Agency chief Mohamed Buba Marwa said a Nigerian national recruited the five to produce meth at an industrial complex in Enugu, where officers recovered 1.5 metric tons of meth, 6.7 tons of chemicals and industrial equipment; the agency says it has now dismantled four industrial-scale meth laboratories, all in the country's south.

stories.headline: South Africa's Ramaphosa wins court case to overturn 'Farmgate' panel report
stories.summary: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa won a court bid on Wednesday to set aside a panel report that had found he may have violated the constitution over misconduct allegations linked to his 'Farmgate' scandal, Reuters reports. The ruling overturns the panel report at the centre of the long-running affair over money stolen from Ramaphosa's game farm.

stories.headline: South African rand eases, with US inflation data in focus
stories.summary: The South African rand weakened on Wednesday to 17.6275 to the dollar, down about 0.5 percent from its previous close, as market participants awaited U.S. inflation figures that could signal the Federal Reserve's next moves, Reuters reports. The U.S. PCE index, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, is the last key inflation release before the Fed's final 2026 meeting, and South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond was steady with a yield of 8.66 percent.

stories.headline: Africa can borrow its way to lower debt burden, OECD and AU say
stories.summary: African countries could lower their debt burdens by borrowing more, provided the money funds projects that boost economic growth, the OECD and the African Union said in a joint report on Wednesday, Reuters reports. The report estimates $93 billion of debt-funded investment in productive assets over five years could raise annual growth by nearly a percentage point, create more than 10 million jobs and cut Africa's debt-to-GDP ratio by 14 percentage points, while warning that 23 of 38 assessed countries are at risk of debt distress.

stories.headline: Nigerian cybersecurity startup Aeon extends pre-seed to $2 million
stories.summary: Nigerian cybersecurity startup Aeon has extended its pre-seed round to $2 million to expand its engineering team and accelerate product development, TechCabal reports. Launch Africa Ventures and Octerra Capital joined existing backers including Terra Industries and Resilience17, the fund founded by Flutterwave co-founder Olugbenga Agboola; Aeon's AI-powered Aeon Console platform and Aeon Edge network device are aimed at African organisations facing AI-enabled cybercrime, which INTERPOL says now enables about 55 percent of reported cybercrimes on the continent.

stories.headline: Viola Davis Calls Out ‘George Floyd’ Musical As Playbill Apologizes For ‘Hateful’ Casting Notice
stories.summary: Viola Davis has spoken out against a proposed George Floyd-inspired musical after a casting notice for the production appeared on Playbill's job board seeking singers and rappers, Black Enterprise reports. Playbill removed the listing and apologised unequivocally, calling it a hateful listing that had no place on its site and saying it is revising its approval processes; Busted Broadway, the company behind the project, defended it as cultural satire rather than mockery of Floyd, who was murdered by Minneapolis police officer Derek Chauvin in 2020.

stories.headline: Jackson State University to Layoff Eight Employees Due to Changes in Title III Funding
stories.summary: Jackson State University is eliminating eight positions, including staff in its division of institutional advancement, because of changes in how its federal Title III funding is allocated, HBCU News reports. The university, which received about $8.2 million in Title III funds in 2022 to support 21 projects through 2027, said the actions result from a compliance-driven reallocation of funds rather than a reduction or cancellation of federal support; the affected employees were told their roles end December 31 and were encouraged to apply for internal vacancies.

stories.headline: Essence Festival Will Not Return To New Orleans In 2027
stories.summary: The Essence Festival of Culture will not return to New Orleans in 2027, ending a run of more than three decades, after Sundial Media Group and city officials failed to reach a new multiyear agreement following the expiration of the previous seven-year contract, Black Enterprise reports. The festival has generated an estimated $300 million in economic impact for the city; Mayor Helena Moreno said New Orleans will develop a new Black cultural celebration for the 2027 Fourth of July weekend, and Essence's next destination has not been announced.

stories.headline: Kwanza Jones, José E. Feliciano, Near Record $750M Deal To Buy LA Sparks
stories.summary: Entrepreneur Kwanza Jones and her husband, investor José E. Feliciano, are in advanced negotiations to buy the Los Angeles Sparks for a reported $750 million, which would be the largest franchise sale in WNBA history, Black Enterprise reports, citing Sportico and NBC Sports. The price is about 25 times the Sparks' 2026 revenue and more than double the previous WNBA record of $300 million; the couple bought baseball's San Diego Padres for $3.9 billion in August, and the Sparks sale is not final and remains subject to league approval.

stories.headline: Killer Mike's Greenwood Banking Program Shuts Down
stories.summary: Greenwood, the digital banking venture co-founded by Killer Mike, Andrew Young and Ryan Glover to expand banking access for Black and Latino communities, has shut down its banking program, Black Enterprise reports. The program ended on November 19 when Greenwood terminated its arrangement with Coastal Community Bank and closed all accounts; remaining balances will be returned by paper check by December 2, customers were asked to confirm mailing addresses by November 24, and a partnership with Ben Crump's DreamFi does not transfer accounts automatically.

stories.headline: 'HBCU First LOOK' Awards $8.5K To Student Filmmakers
stories.summary: Three student filmmakers shared $8,500 in awards at the fourth annual HBCU First LOOK Film & TV Festival at Howard University on November 5-7, which drew more than 450 submissions to its 2026 Film Challenge, Black Enterprise reports. Florida A&M's Jada Davis won the $5,000 grand prize for a documentary on Black landownership, Howard's Mya Delgado took $2,500 for the short 'Flowers,' and Coppin State's Christian Sutton earned $1,000 for 'My Alter Ego.'

stories.headline: Stephen A. Smith says Black NBA players have thanked him over white Lakers comments
stories.summary: ESPN personality Stephen A. Smith said on his 'Straight Shooter' show on Tuesday that Black NBA players have privately thanked him for his comments questioning whether the league's Black stars would let the Los Angeles Lakers, led by white stars Luka Dončić, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler, win a championship, the New York Post reports. Smith doubled down on the take despite the Lakers' 15-3 start, while former Celtics champion Kevin Garnett pushed back on him on their joint show.

stories.headline: A&T Will Take on Southern in 2026 Red Lobster Band of the Year Finals
stories.summary: North Carolina A&T's Blue & Gold Marching Machine will face Southern University's Human Jukebox for the Division I national Red Lobster Band of the Year title on December 11 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, as part of Celebration Bowl weekend, the university announced on November 24. A&T also announced a historic $5 million investment in the band's practice and support facilities, including a new practice field and facility modernisation, in the band's first year under interim director Aaron Campbell.

stories.headline: CAS ruling in favour of Senegal reasserts that referee's decision is final
stories.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has upheld Senegal's appeal and reinstated them as Africa Cup of Nations winners, finding referee Jean-Jacques Ndala committed no error of law when he resumed January's final after Senegal's 14-minute walk-off protest, Reuters reports. CAF's Appeal Board had ruled Senegal forfeited the match to Morocco under article 82, but CAS secretary general Matthieu Reeb said the panel found the referee did not commit any error of law, reasserting that a referee's decision on facts of play is final.

stories.headline: Nigeria's Tinubu asks lawmakers to trim 2026 budget spending
stories.summary: Nigeria's President Bola Tinubu has asked parliament to cut 2026 federal budget spending to 65.2 trillion naira ($48 billion) from the 68.3 trillion naira lawmakers approved earlier this year, Reuters reports. In a letter seen by Reuters on Tuesday, Tinubu said the revised plan aligns with existing obligations and available resources and would keep the fiscal deficit unchanged at 5.64 percent of GDP; the finance minister is expected to present the 2027 budget next month.

stories.headline: Nigeria's central bank maintains key rate to anchor inflation expectations
stories.summary: Nigeria's central bank kept its monetary policy rate unchanged at 23 percent on Tuesday, Governor Olayemi Cardoso said, a decision the bank said would help anchor inflation expectations, Reuters reports. Six of seven economists polled by Reuters had expected the hold, which follows a surprise 350-basis-point cut in September; headline inflation eased to 14.06 percent year-on-year in October from 14.63 percent in September.

stories.headline: Commanders rally past Bengals as last-minute drive produces winning FG
stories.summary: Jayden Daniels led Washington 64 yards in 34 seconds with two throws to rookie Antonio Williams, setting up Drew Stevens' fifth field goal, a 26-yarder as time expired, in a 22-20 Monday night win over Cincinnati in Landover. Daniels threw for 289 yards and ran for 55, Williams had nine catches for 122 yards, and the Commanders improved to 4-5-1 while ending the Bengals' five-game winning streak and dropping them to 7-3.

stories.headline: Moroccan federation reports incident to CAS during Senegal AFCON appeal, source says
stories.summary: Morocco's football federation has reported an incident to the Court of Arbitration for Sport during Senegal's appeal over the Africa Cup of Nations title, ahead of a ruling due later on Tuesday, a source with direct knowledge told Reuters. The federation alleges Senegal Football Federation president Abdoulaye Fall spoke by phone on Sunday with one of the three arbitrators hearing the case; Reuters could not independently verify whether the call took place, and CAS was not immediately available for comment.

stories.headline: South African rand steady ahead of leading indicator data
stories.summary: The South African rand was steady in early trade on Tuesday at 17.4125 to the dollar, little changed from its previous close of 17.41, as investors awaited the central bank's leading business cycle indicator for September. The Reserve Bank release covers vehicle sales, business confidence and money supply, markets are also awaiting U.S. PCE inflation data on Wednesday, and South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond was flat with a yield of 8.65 percent.

stories.headline: South Africa's Pepkor warns port disruptions to weigh on festive trading
stories.summary: South African retailer Pepkor has warned that port disruptions and delayed inventory arrivals will weigh on near-term trading heading into Black Friday and the festive season, even as it reported a 9.7 percent rise in annual normalised headline earnings. Revenue rose 11.9 percent to 105.9 billion rand for the year ended September 30, normalised headline earnings per share climbed to 177.5 cents, and the Pep and Ackermans owner said its discount model gained more than 200 basis points of market share.

stories.headline: Ackerman hits quickfire 150 as South Africa take 137-run lead
stories.summary: South Africa opener Marques Ackerman raced to 150 off 138 balls with 27 boundaries to establish a 137-run lead over Bangladesh at lunch on day two of the second test at Centurion. Ackerman, trapped leg-before by Shoriful Islam, scored his second successive test century after 157 in last week's nine-wicket first test win, and South Africa reached 228-3 in reply to Bangladesh's 91 after resuming on 88-1.

stories.headline: FIFA President Says Nigeria Is Not Ready. ACG Says the Problem Is Not Nigeria. It Is the Model.
stories.summary: FIFA president Gianni Infantino told ARISE News in Abuja on November 23 that Nigeria could not host a World Cup today, citing inadequate stadiums, airports and transport, and African Collaborations Group founder Nicolas Pompigne-Mognard responded that the problem is the model, not Nigeria. ACG argues standalone football-only stadiums sit empty some 340 days a year and urges integrated sport and entertainment districts that generate revenue year-round, a direction backed by a new World Bank, IOC and AFD report on sport in Africa.

stories.headline: Tuskegee University Global Campus Begins Accepting Students in January
stories.summary: Tuskegee University's new Global Campus will begin accepting students in January, expanding the HBCU's online reach with 7.5-week terms across fall, spring and summer designed for working adults, parents, veterans and learners for whom in-person study is cost-prohibitive, the university announced on November 23. Tuskegee already offers online degrees including a BS in Animal, Poultry, and Veterinary Sciences, an MS in Social Work and a Ph.D. in Integrative Public Policy and Development, with five new degree programs planned for Fall 2027.

stories.headline: Drake State Partners With Blue Origin for New Opportunities in Space Manufacturing
stories.summary: Historically Black Drake State Community and Technical College in Huntsville, Alabama, has partnered with Blue Origin to prepare students for space manufacturing careers through ATLAS, a registered apprenticeship combining classroom instruction with hands-on training at Blue Origin facilities. A first cohort of 10 students began in October, earning full-time salaries and benefits from day one and a path to nationally recognised journey worker certifications in skills including CNC programming and quality systems.

stories.headline: NCAA Mandatory Coach Handshake Nixed After Dawn Staley-Geno Auriemma Clash
stories.summary: The NCAA is removing the mandatory pregame handshake for coaches in the women's basketball tournament, following the heated April Final Four exchange between South Carolina coach Dawn Staley and UConn coach Geno Auriemma, Black Enterprise reports. A Division I women's basketball committee memo distributed on Friday makes the handshake optional while still encouraging an informal greeting, and also ends mandatory media locker room access between the Sweet 16 and Elite Eight.

stories.headline: NFL Legend And ESPN Broadcaster Tom Jackson Dies At 75
stories.summary: Former Denver Broncos linebacker and longtime ESPN analyst Tom Jackson has died at 75, his family confirmed to ESPN; he died on Friday, November 20, and Chris Berman announced the news on Sunday NFL Countdown, with no cause disclosed. Jackson played 14 seasons as a cornerstone of Denver's Orange Crush defence, earned three Pro Bowl selections, and then helped define ESPN's NFL coverage for nearly three decades alongside Berman on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown.

stories.headline: Texas Southern Fires Head Football Coach Cris Dishman
stories.summary: Texas Southern is parting ways with head football coach Cris Dishman, athletic director Ashley Robinson confirmed, after the Tigers closed 2026 at 3-8 overall and 2-6 in the SWAC with a 42-17 loss to Arkansas-Pine Bluff. Dishman went 14-19 in three seasons, including the program's first winning season since 2000 in 2025, and the university said on November 23 that he will not return for 2027 and that a nationwide search will begin immediately.

stories.headline: Stacey Abrams Expands Mission Beyond Voting Rights
stories.summary: Stacey Abrams is restructuring Fair Fight, the voting rights organisation she founded in 2018, to wind down its voting-focused operations and unveil a new mission in 2027 focused on protecting democratic institutions, Black Enterprise reports, citing the Associated Press. Abrams said the shift reflects concerns over congressional redistricting and state government authority, and that the group will educate Americans on how state legislatures shape health care, education and spending, without abandoning voting rights advocacy.

stories.headline: Oprah Daily to close at year’s end; Winfrey offers departing staff $20,000
stories.summary: Oprah Daily will close on December 31, ending Oprah Winfrey's 26-year publishing partnership with Hearst Magazines that began with O, The Oprah Magazine in 2000, Editor and Publisher reports. Winfrey will personally give $20,000 to more than two dozen affected employees, on top of Hearst severance, according to Axios reporting cited in the story; employees were notified of the closure on November 18.

stories.headline: Ghana make history as Black Challenge beat Morocco to win 2026 Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico
stories.summary: Ghana's Black Challenge have won the 2026 Amputee Football World Cup, beating Morocco 1-0 in Sunday's final in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico, for the country's first world title in amputee football. Captain Richard Opentil scored the decisive goal in the 32nd minute, forward Mubarik Mohammed took the Golden Boot with seven goals, and Ghana became the second African nation to win the competition after Angola in 2018, having beaten defending champions Turkey on penalties in the semi-final.

stories.headline: Qualcomm Awards $75,000 to African Livestock AI Startup Qualikeeper as 2026 Accelerator Concludes
stories.summary: Qualcomm has awarded a $75,000 equity-free grant to African agritech startup Qualikeeper Investments to expand StocKeeper, its AI-powered internet-of-things platform for monitoring livestock health, TechMoran reports. Qualikeeper won the 2026 Qualcomm for Good Social Impact Fund at the close of the fourth Make in Africa Startup Mentorship Program, beating nine other startups from nine African countries working on AI, edge computing and connected devices, and will also receive tailored technical assistance.

stories.headline: 'The Honorable' Shyne Will Always 'Rock The Bells' And Rep Belize
stories.summary: Grammy-nominated rapper and former Belizean opposition leader Moses 'Shyne' Barrow is preparing to perform at LL Cool J's Rock the Bells Festival on November 29 in Newark while laying the groundwork for a new album, a 2027 memoir and a 2030 return to Belize's Parliament, Black Enterprise reports. Barrow, the only hip-hop artist elected to a national congress-level parliament, told the magazine there is no difference between Shyne the performer and Moses the parliamentarian, and that he brings the same energy to the legislature.

stories.headline: Major Banks Warn Customers Could Be Liable For AI Mistakes
stories.summary: Major U.S. banks including JPMorgan Chase, Citi and Ally are warning customers that they could be held financially responsible for mistakes made by AI agents they let access their accounts, Black Enterprise reports. Citi has updated its online user agreement to say customers who authorize third-party AI agents are responsible for activity conducted through those tools, and the banks are also warning against sharing passwords and security codes with AI platforms, though the warnings do not override federal consumer protection laws.

stories.headline: Zambia opposition leader charged with attempting to overthrow government
stories.summary: Zambian opposition leader Brian Mundubile and more than a dozen associates have been charged with trying to overthrow the government and committed to the High Court to stand trial for treason, according to a charge sheet read in court on Monday. Mundubile and his running mate Makebi Zulu, who say the August presidential election was rigged, are accused of plotting between April and August and of funding military training in Russia for five people; Mundubile says he is innocent and the charges are politically motivated, and the trial is expected early next year.

stories.headline: Fields of graves: Hidden deaths reveal scale of Ebola disaster
stories.summary: A Reuters investigation using satellite imagery of cemeteries in Bunia, eastern Congo, estimates the Ebola outbreak's true toll is far above official figures: by early November the city's excess deaths topped 1,000, more than 50 percent higher than the official Ebola tally of 707, in an outbreak that has infected more than 11,500 people and killed over 5,500 nationwide. Africa CDC's head of emergency response called the findings broadly plausible, while Congo's health ministry did not respond to requests for comment.

stories.headline: Congo halts cobalt exports again to tackle oversupply, support prices, industry regulator says
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo will suspend all cobalt exports from November 30 until further notice, its strategic minerals regulator ARECOMS said on Monday, in a second halt since April 2025 aimed at tackling oversupply, weak prices and rising inventories. The suspension covers industrial and artisanal production alike, and ARECOMS says the pause will be used to adjust its quota system, with a review four months after it takes effect and no automatic resumption.

stories.headline: Coca-Cola HBC makes JSE debut as CCBA deal nears completion
stories.summary: Coca-Cola HBC shares began trading on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Monday in one of the largest inward listings in recent years, days before the bottler completes its acquisition of a 75 percent controlling stake in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa, the continent's largest Coca-Cola bottler. The Swiss-based company, already listed in London and Athens with a market value of about 341 billion rand, opened at 996 rand; after the deal closes on November 27 it will account for about two-thirds of Coca-Cola system volumes in Africa.

stories.headline: CAS to release Senegal Africa Cup of Nations title appeal decision on Tuesday
stories.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport will announce on Tuesday its decision on Senegal's appeal against being stripped of this year's Africa Cup of Nations title, the court said on Monday. Senegal beat hosts Morocco 1-0 after extra time in January's final but were later ruled to have forfeited the match by walking off the pitch in protest at a late penalty, with CAF awarding Morocco a 3-0 win; Senegal argue the referee's decision to complete the match was final.

stories.headline: Springboks make seven changes for Nations Championship final
stories.summary: South Africa have made seven changes and one positional swap for Sunday's Nations Championship final against France at Twickenham, with DR Congo-born loose-forward Emmanuel Tshituka in line for a debut off the bench. Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu moves to fullback for the injured Damian Willemse, Manie Libbok starts at flyhalf and captain Siya Kolisi again leads the back row; France beat the Springboks 21-19 in Paris earlier this month.

stories.headline: South Africans Marx, Nche shortlisted for world player of the year award
stories.summary: Springboks hooker Malcolm Marx, last year's winner, and prop Ox Nche have been named on the four-man shortlist for World Rugby's men's player of the year award, World Rugby said on Monday, with Nche bidding to become the first prop to win it. France winger Louis Bielle-Biarrey and New Zealand centre Jordie Barrett complete the list, South Africa's Paul de Villiers is shortlisted for breakthrough player of the year, and the winners will be announced during this weekend's Nations Championship Finals at Twickenham.

stories.headline: South African rand gains as commodity prices rise and dollar weakens
stories.summary: The South African rand strengthened about 0.9 percent on Monday to trade at 17.4325 against the dollar, helped by firmer commodity prices, with gold recovering from a 14-month low and platinum up 1.2 percent, and by a softer dollar. South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond also firmed, its yield falling 7.5 basis points to 8.63 percent, as traders looked ahead to U.S. inflation data on Wednesday.

stories.headline: Launch Africa Leads $500,000 into AI Commerce Startup Khaime
stories.summary: Launch Africa Ventures has led a $500,000 pre-seed investment in Khaime, an AI commerce startup founded by Gabriel Olokunwolu that lets merchants build AI-generated online stores, take payments in more than 120 currencies and automate customer conversations across WhatsApp, Instagram and Messenger. Khaime says it has attracted more than 5,000 merchants and that its AI sales assistant recovered 32.3 percent of abandoned carts in October; the startup has also been selected for the Visa Africa FinTech Accelerator.

stories.headline: Michael Vick gets first conference win as Norfolk State completes four-game turnaround
stories.summary: Michael Vick has his first conference win as Norfolk State head coach, as the Spartans beat Howard 35-7 in Saturday's season finale to close 2026 at 5-7, a four-game improvement on his 1-11 debut season. Norfolk State snapped a 10-game MEAC losing streak behind two fourth-quarter pick-sixes seven seconds apart, a career-high 183 rushing yards from Jalyn Daniels and 460 yards of total offence, for the program's highest win total since 2021.

stories.headline: Prescott accounts for 5 TDs as Cowboys roll to 51-30 victory over Titans
stories.summary: Dak Prescott threw four touchdown passes and ran for a fifth as Dallas beat Tennessee 51-30 in Arlington on Sunday, scoring touchdowns on its first six drives and on every possession before a closing kneel-down. Prescott finished 28 of 33 for 325 yards with a franchise-record-tying 19 straight completions, while CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens each topped 100 receiving yards and scored; Dallas improved to 5-6 and Tennessee fell to 1-9.

stories.headline: HBCU Bands Honor Scott Colom at Soul Bowl
stories.summary: Alcorn State's Sounds of Dyn-O-Mite and Jackson State's Sonic Boom of the South set aside their Soul Bowl band rivalry at halftime in Lorman to join forces and spell out the name of Senator-elect Scott Colom, the first Black Mississippian elected to the U.S. Senate by statewide popular vote. The tribute, less than two weeks after the Associated Press called Colom's win over incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith, played out on the campus first led by Hiram Revels, the first Black U.S. senator.

stories.headline: Chadwick Boseman's father Leroy dies at 82
stories.summary: Leroy Boseman, father of the late Black Panther star Chadwick Boseman, has died at 82 after a brief illness, his family confirmed; he passed away on Thursday, November 19, in Belton, South Carolina, where he had worked in a textile factory and run an upholstery shop while raising three sons with his wife Carolyn, a nurse. The death comes six years after Chadwick's death at 43 and days before what would have been his 50th birthday.

stories.headline: HBCU Football Coaching Tracker 2026
stories.summary: Five HBCU football programs have head coaching vacancies as of November 22, the HBCU Legends tracker reports, each led by an interim coach: Bethune-Cookman, the only Division I opening, where Alvin 'Shine' Wyatt stepped in for the Florida Classic, plus Tuskegee, Lane College and Fort Valley State in the SIAC and Lincoln University of Missouri in the GLVC. Stillman College, by contrast, has hired Teddy Keaton as coach and athletic director to restart a program idle since 2015.

stories.headline: Death toll from Nigeria boat accident rises to 24
stories.summary: At least 24 people have died after a crowded boat carrying passengers to a funeral capsized in southern Nigeria on Friday, the National Emergency Management Agency said, with 24 bodies recovered and 24 survivors rescued as search and rescue work continued on Saturday. The boat was travelling from Ayama to the Ukubie community in Bayelsa State for a burial ceremony when it went down; police had earlier put the toll at four and cited a mechanical failure, and Bayelsa governor Douye Diri visited the scene and ordered an investigation.

stories.headline: South Africa make two changes for second test against Bangladesh
stories.summary: South Africa have made two changes for the second and final test against Bangladesh in Centurion on Monday, bringing in batter Tony de Zorzi and fast bowler Anrich Nortje as they look to close out the series. De Zorzi replaces regular captain Temba Bavuma, who has a calf injury, with Aiden Markram again standing in as skipper, while Nortje comes in for Dane Paterson; South Africa won the first test by nine wickets and sit top of the World Test Championship table as defending champions.

stories.headline: UMaT's First Ghanaian Female Valedictorian: Anna Hannah Ansah
stories.summary: Anna Hannah Ansah has become the University of Mines and Technology's first Ghanaian female valedictorian, graduating in Petroleum Engineering with a Cumulative Weighted Average of 91.02 percent and collecting six awards at the university's 19th Congregation in Tarkwa. The Wesley Girls' High School alumna took honours including the Gold Fields Ghana Award for Overall Best Graduating Student, and is completing her national service at the Ghana National Petroleum Corporation in Tema.

stories.headline: Lesotho Sends 63 Young Basotho to the 2026 YouthConnekt Africa Summit in Rwanda
stories.summary: Lesotho has flagged off 63 young innovators and entrepreneurs to represent the country at the YouthConnekt Africa Summit in Kigali, Rwanda, from November 25 to 27, the largest delegation from a single country in the summit's history. Prime Minister Ntsokoane Samuel Matekane handed over the national flag at the send-off in Maseru, describing young Basotho as the country's greatest national asset, with the delegation backed by the SEBABATSO youth empowerment initiative.

stories.headline: SC State Closes Regular Season Unbeaten in MEAC Play With 26-16 Win Over Delaware State
stories.summary: South Carolina State beat Delaware State 26-16 in Orangeburg to close the regular season 10-2 and a perfect 5-0 in the MEAC, the Bulldogs' third straight conference title and 21st overall. Tied 16-16 in the fourth quarter, SC State pulled away on a Jett Jackson field goal and a Josh Shaw touchdown run; quarterback Keely Watson threw the 100th touchdown pass of his career, and head coach Chennis Berry is now 15-0 in MEAC play ahead of the December 12 Celebration Bowl.

stories.headline: Navy won't rename Doris Miller aircraft carrier after Trump
stories.summary: The Navy has confirmed it will keep the name USS Doris Miller on the Ford-class carrier CVN-81, ending reports that it considered renaming the ship for President Donald Trump; a Navy statement on November 21 said there is no intention to change the name, and a keel-laying ceremony is set for December 5 at Newport News. Miller, the Pearl Harbor hero who would be the first African American and first enlisted sailor to have a carrier named for him, remains the subject of a family-backed push for a posthumous Medal of Honor.

stories.headline: Former Jackson Mayor Chokwe Antar Lumumba sentenced in FBI bribery case
stories.summary: Former Jackson, Mississippi mayor Chokwe Antar Lumumba has been sentenced to 37 months in federal prison, the last of three officials sentenced in an FBI undercover bribery sting built around a proposed downtown hotel. Judge Daniel P. Jordan III also ordered one year of supervised release and the forfeiture of the $50,000 Lumumba took from undercover agents posing as developers in exchange for moving a bidding deadline; Lumumba, who served as mayor from 2017 to 2025 and pleaded guilty to conspiracy in July, is to report to prison on January 4, 2027.

stories.headline: Prairie View wins division will host SWAC Championship
stories.summary: Prairie View A&M beat Alabama State 45-10 in Montgomery on Saturday to win its second straight SWAC West Division title, its fifth win in a row after a shaky October, and home-field advantage for the SWAC Championship Game. The Panthers will host Alabama A&M, which clinched the East with a 51-19 win over Mississippi Valley State, on December 5 at Panther Stadium, with the winner advancing to face MEAC champion South Carolina State in the Celebration Bowl on December 12.

stories.headline: HBCUs swept out of opening round of NCAA Playoffs
stories.summary: All six HBCU football programs in the NCAA Division II playoff field lost their first-round games on Saturday, ending a historic postseason in which the SIAC placed a record four teams and the CIAA two. Top seed Benedict fell 38-3 at home to Newberry, Kentucky State lost 42-14 to Carson-Newman, Edward Waters lost 56-26 at Valdosta State in its playoff debut, Central State lost 42-23 to UNC Pembroke in its first appearance since 1986, Virginia Union lost 31-14 to California (PA) and Fayetteville State lost 34-13 to Kutztown.

stories.headline: FAMU Takes the Florida Classic from BCU
stories.summary: Florida A&M beat Bethune-Cookman 27-14 in the Florida Classic at Camping World Stadium in Orlando on Saturday, in front of 51,345 fans, to reclaim the rivalry trophy. Freshman quarterback Armond Parker ran for 105 yards and a touchdown, threw for another score and was named the game's Most Valuable Player, while the Rattlers' defense forced five turnovers and held the Wildcats without an offensive touchdown until late in the fourth quarter.

stories.headline: Tigers Handle Tougaloo to Close Homestand, 96-60
stories.summary: Stillman College's men's basketball team never trailed in a 96-60 win over Tougaloo College in Tuscaloosa on Saturday, closing out the East/West HBCU Athletic Conference Pod at Birthright Alumni Hall. LaMarcus Crawford led the Tigers with 22 points on 8-for-10 shooting, A'Dreline Robinson added 17 points, 11 assists and four steals, and Michael Kinnard scored 16 as Stillman opened the game with a 10-2 run and built a 23-4 lead inside six minutes.

stories.headline: Black Challenge stun defending champions Turkey to storm historic World Cup Final
stories.summary: Ghana's Black Challenge amputee football team have reached the Amputee Football World Cup final for the first time, eliminating defending champions Turkey 4-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw following extra time in Mexico. Mubarik Mohammed scored in extra time to take his tournament tally to seven goals before converting again in the shootout, and Ghana will face Morocco, who came back to beat Brazil 2-1, in an all-African final in San Juan de los Lagos on Sunday.

stories.headline: Samia: New constitution ready by 2028/29
stories.summary: Tanzania should have a new or revised constitution by 2028 or 2029, President Samia Suluhu Hassan has said, as her government prepares to establish a Reconciliation Commission to gather views ahead of the reform process. Speaking to senior police officers in Moshi on November 20, Samia said nominations were being sought from religious leaders, political parties and civil society groups to serve on the commission, which will identify the areas of the constitution that need to change.

stories.headline: Kenya flags off eight ICT students for Huawei training in China
stories.summary: Kenya has flagged off eight university students for Huawei's Seeds for the Future 2026 programme in Shenzhen and Dongguan, China, up from five students sent in 2025. The fully funded training at Huawei's research and development facilities covers artificial intelligence, 5G and 6G networks, cloud computing and digital power, and Principal Secretary Korir Sing'Oei linked the cohort to the government's Digital Superhighway agenda and its push to connect education to skills and jobs.

stories.headline: Kenya: PS Oluga Explores Opportunities for AI in Healthcare Delivery
stories.summary: Kenya's Principal Secretary for Medical Services, Dr Ouma Oluga, has hosted Anthropic's global health team lead Anne Stake in Nairobi to explore using artificial intelligence to strengthen healthcare delivery. The talks, distributed by APO Group on behalf of the Ministry of Health, covered AI support for clinical decision-making, disease surveillance and diagnostic efficiency under Kenya's national AI in Health Strategy, with an emphasis on data sovereignty, security and responsible use.

stories.headline: GTEC Urges University of Mines and Technology to Lead Technological Fight Against Galamsey
stories.summary: Ghana's Tertiary Education Commission has challenged the University of Mines and Technology in Tarkwa to lead the development of technological solutions to illegal small-scale mining, known as galamsey. Director-General Professor Abdullah Jinapor told the university's 19th Congregation that enforcement alone cannot win the fight, urging research into mercury-free gold recovery, land reclamation technology and digital monitoring systems, with collaboration across academia, government, mining companies and affected communities.

stories.headline: Most new Black Democrats in decades to join US Congress, set to sway policy, party
stories.summary: The largest class of new Black Democratic lawmakers in more than 30 years will join Congress in January, a Reuters analysis finds, with 13 new Black Democratic members, the biggest cohort since 1993, despite Republican-led redistricting. Black candidates won 58 House seats, Senate Black representation reached a record seven, and the Congressional Black Caucus will enter the session with a record 64 members, setting up a test of whether the numbers translate into power on voting rights, health care and economic inequality.

stories.headline: America elects record 5 Black governors. How did they make history?
stories.summary: Five Black governors will serve at once for the first time after the November 3 elections, USA TODAY reports: Nevada's Aaron Ford, Florida's Bryon Donalds, Wisconsin's David Crowley, Georgia's Keisha Lance Bottoms, the nation's first Black woman governor, and Maryland's re-elected Wes Moore. Only three Black Americans had ever been elected governor before this cycle, the winners centred their campaigns on affordability, and the Democratic Governors Association and its allies spent more than $70 million backing the Democratic winners.

stories.headline: Black organizers turn Southern upsets into power play
stories.summary: Black organisers are moving to turn a wave of Southern midterm surprises into lasting power, building a bench of Black, multiracial and working-class candidates from school boards to statehouses, ENM News reports. In South Carolina, Democrats flipped 10 House seats, seven won by Black candidates, ending the GOP supermajority, and the Working Families Party plans recruitment events in Georgia, Tennessee, South Carolina and Mississippi in early 2027, aiming through its Southern Made effort to prepare 1,000 working-class candidates by 2030.

stories.headline: Gwinnett's first Black police chief to retire after 30 years; deputy chief Steven Shaw named successor
stories.summary: Gwinnett County Police Chief James D. McClure, who became the Georgia county's first Black police chief in 2021, will retire after 30 years with the department, county officials announced on Friday. Deputy Chief Steven K. Shaw, a 29-year veteran who commands the Operations Bureau and previously led the Homicide and Robbery Unit, has been appointed to succeed him and will take over on December 20.

stories.headline: Ravens announce Marlon Humphrey decision after Baltimore podcast joke
stories.summary: The Baltimore Ravens have sent cornerback Marlon Humphrey home and will keep him inactive for Sunday's game at Carolina, a one-game penalty for now, after a podcast joke that Baltimore is best at making criminals. Coach Jesse Minter said the decision followed internal talks including the team's 10-player leadership council, while Mayor Brandon Scott said a verbal apology is not enough, arguing young Black boys in the city look to Ravens players as role models, and invited Humphrey to meet residents working to steer others away from past mistakes.

stories.headline: South Africa's first female deputy president and UN official dies
stories.summary: Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, South Africa's first female deputy president, who also served as UN under-secretary-general and executive director of UN Women, has died at the age of 71, the presidency said late on Friday. A former teacher first elected to parliament in 1994, she served as deputy president from 2005 to 2008, overseeing poverty-reduction initiatives with a focus on women, after roles as minister of minerals and energy and deputy trade minister, and led UN Women for two terms from 2013.

stories.headline: CAF endorses Infantino for re-election as FIFA president
stories.summary: Confederation of African Football president Patrice Motsepe has again endorsed Gianni Infantino for re-election as FIFA president, speaking at CAF's Ordinary General Assembly in Abuja, Nigeria, on Saturday on behalf of its 54 member associations. Infantino confirmed grants to member associations will more than triple under FIFA Forward 4.0, from $8 million over four years to $25 million from January 2027, and pledged to keep developing football in Africa at the forefront of his agenda.

stories.headline: Kofi Adams debunks claims of neglecting Black Challenge team
stories.summary: Ghana's Sports Minister Kofi Adams has rejected claims that he abandoned the Black Challenge amputee football team at the World Cup in Mexico, saying he initiated the Gold Fields Ghana sponsorship talks in February and followed the team's progress throughout. Adams said NPC Ghana confirmed each delegation member will receive $8,000 in Gold Fields funding for per diems and bonuses, while Tafo MP Ekow Assafuah Vincent and the team's technical director Ali Jarra questioned why the minister had not visited the semi-finalists in Mexico as he did the Black Stars.

stories.headline: JaBBEM’s Damion Coombs Slams PM Holness’s Beach Plan, Calling Two Beaches Per Parish “Ludicrous”
stories.summary: Damion Coombs of the Jamaica Beach Birthright Environmental Movement has called Prime Minister Andrew Holness's pledge of at least two free public beaches per parish, with 10 beaches upgraded, ludicrous, arguing all of Jamaica's coastline is a birthright, not a limited privilege. JaBBEM, which says less than one percent of the coastline remains freely accessible, is demanding repeal of the colonial-era Beach Control Act of 1956, withdrawal of the proposed Beach Access and Management Policy, and a law declaring the entire coastline a public common.

stories.headline: James Harden erupts for 51 to pass Kobe Bryant on 50-point games list
stories.summary: James Harden scored 51 points on Friday night to lead the Cleveland Cavaliers past the Indiana Pacers 128-119 in an NBA Cup game, his 26th career 50-point game. The 37-year-old's performance moved him past Kobe Bryant into third place on the all-time list for 50-point games, behind only Michael Jordan with 31 and Wilt Chamberlain with 118, and was his highest-scoring game of the season.

stories.headline: HBCU women's basketball: Alabama A&M makes history with UAB upset
stories.summary: Alabama A&M's women's basketball team beat UAB 66-53 in Huntsville for the first win over the Blazers in program history, handing the previously unbeaten team its first loss of the season. The Bulldogs outscored UAB 23-9 in the third quarter and held them to 27.1 percent shooting, with Alisha Murray scoring 15 points with five rebounds and six steals, Janessa Kelley adding 14 points and Aniya Palmer recording a double-double.

stories.headline: Prosecutor declines to charge Wisconsin police officer who fatally shot a Black man
stories.summary: A Wisconsin prosecutor has declined to charge the Madison police officer who shot and killed Corey Ruiz, a 38-year-old Black man, in July, finding the officer acted reasonably after Ruiz resisted, produced a knife and was unaffected by Taser rounds. The decision drew immediate condemnation from Ruiz's family and advocates; civil rights attorney Ben Crump said the video showed unjustified force, family members held a candlelight vigil, and Wisconsin Governor-elect David Crowley called the killing deeply troubling while urging peaceful protest.

stories.headline: Bowie State University Announces Karine Jean-Pierre as 2026 Winter Commencement Keynote Speaker
stories.summary: Bowie State University will welcome Karine Jean-Pierre, the former White House press secretary and senior adviser to President Joe Biden, as keynote speaker for its 2026 Winter Commencement on December 18. Jean-Pierre, who in 2022 became the first Black person and first openly queer person to serve as White House press secretary, will address graduates at the Leonidas S. James Physical Education Complex, encouraging them to pursue their ambitions, serve their communities and lead with purpose.

stories.headline: Artist Aaron Douglas’ ‘Harriet Tubman’ Painting Sells At Sotheby’s For $14.4M
stories.summary: Harlem Renaissance artist Aaron Douglas's 1931 painting Harriet Tubman sold at Sotheby's on November 18 for $14,480,000, far above its $2.5 million to $3.5 million estimate and a new auction record for the artist. Bennett College, the historically Black women's college in Greensboro that has held the painting since it was commissioned for it, sold the work to fund its Women's Health Initiative, though some students and alumnae opposed the sale of the heritage piece.

stories.headline: Bristling Springboks won't be 'broken' by Erasmus ban
stories.summary: South Africa captain Siya Kolisi has pushed back at a suggestion that coach Rassie Erasmus was being dramatic about letting the country down in defeat by France, as the Springboks vowed not to be sidetracked by Erasmus's six-match ban for criticising match officials. Assistant coach Mzwandile Stick said Erasmus had been hands-on all week before Saturday's Nations Championship clash with Ireland in Dublin and that no one would break the team, while Kolisi stressed how much representing every South African means to the players.

stories.headline: Scientists are learning more about the rare Ebola virus in Congo outbreak
stories.summary: Scientists are learning more about the rare Bundibugyo Ebola virus behind the Democratic Republic of Congo outbreak, which has passed 11,000 cases and 5,500 deaths in more than six months, with no licensed treatments or vaccines for this species. WHO and Africa CDC officials told Reuters bleeding occurs in only about 5 to 10 percent of confirmed cases, making the disease easier to confuse with malaria, children under five have been hit hardest with 1,207 confirmed cases and 844 deaths, and trials of vaccines and antivirals are now under way.

stories.headline: Myanmar genocide judgment may bolster Gaza case against Israel
stories.summary: The International Court of Justice's landmark ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya will strengthen South Africa's genocide case against Israel over Gaza, legal experts told Reuters, establishing that genocidal intent can coexist with a military objective. South Africa's Foreign Minister Ronald Lamola welcomed the judgment, the first time the court has found a state committed genocide, and said South Africa would study it carefully for its own case, which is not expected to be argued until 2029.

stories.headline: Kwame Afrobics, pioneering London fitness instructor, dies
stories.summary: London's Caribbean and fitness communities are mourning Leroy Kwame McMillan, known as Kwame Afrobics and Mr Socarobics, who died on Sunday, November 15. Kwame founded Afrobics, a pioneering approach that fused fitness with Caribbean music, movement and culture, and through Afrobics and Socarobics encouraged generations to embrace movement while celebrating Caribbean rhythms, Soca News reports.

stories.headline: Peralta Colleges joins effort to bring historically Black college to Oakland
stories.summary: The Peralta Colleges Board of Trustees has unanimously approved a memorandum of understanding with the Oakland HBCU Initiative to explore bringing a historically Black college campus to Oakland, which would be the first HBCU undergraduate presence on the West Coast. A feasibility study released this month estimates a satellite campus, where students could start at a Peralta community college and finish an HBCU degree locally, could add 1,760 Black professionals a year in Oakland and $158 million in annual local spending.

stories.headline: HBCU Students Secure $15K For App Helping Gen Z Build Financial Literacy
stories.summary: Three University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff students, David Adedeji, Nicholas Nettey and Angel Yuzya, have won $15,000 and the top prize at the inaugural Future of XYZ HBCU Innovation Challenge for Brix, a financial coaching app for first-generation and first-year students. Built during AfroTech week in Houston against teams from more than 30 HBCUs, Brix helps students manage financial aid refunds and first paychecks and practise investing with simulated money.

stories.headline: St. Louis advocates challenge HBCU funding gaps
stories.summary: Five St. Louis advocates behind the 1890 Project are suing Missouri over what federal figures put at a $361.6 million funding gap for Lincoln University, the state's 1890 land-grant HBCU, between 1987 and 2020. Their October 7 lawsuit, filed for seven current and former Lincoln students, seeks about $549 million for a court-supervised remedial fund, and the group says it is negotiating with other 1890 institutions and treats litigation as a last resort.

stories.headline: SC State launching first HBCU vet and animal science bachelor's in SC
stories.summary: South Carolina State University has state approval to reopen its bachelor's degree in animal and veterinary sciences, closed in 1971 after 75 years, with pre-veterinary and industry pathways and hands-on lab and farm training. If national accreditation follows, SC State would be South Carolina's first HBCU offering the degree, in a profession where Black people are about 1.3 percent of veterinary professionals, backed by more than $26 million invested in Nance Hall and its research farm.

stories.headline: ‘HBCUs Create Leaders’: America’s First Black Woman Governor is Florida A&M Alum
stories.summary: Georgia Governor-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms, a Florida A&M graduate, became the first Black woman elected governor in U.S. history on November 3, and HBCU leaders say her win, built on healthcare, housing, safety, schools and free community and technical college tuition, is proof of what HBCUs produce. UNCF president Michael Lomax predicted a surge in HBCU applications, saying HBCUs create leaders, while FAMU president Marva Johnson called Bottoms an example of leadership grounded in courage and service.

stories.headline: NCDHHS Office of Rural Health Celebrates National Rural Health Day, Honors NC's 'Community Star' Recipient
stories.summary: Eva Clayton, who in 1992 became the first Black member of Congress from North Carolina since George Henry White in 1898, has been named North Carolina's Community Star for 2026 by the state health department's Office of Rural Health for National Rural Health Day. Clayton, who later served with the UN Food and Agriculture Organization, continues rural health advocacy through the Green Rural Redevelopment Organization and the Eva Clayton Rural Food Institute she founded.

stories.headline: Angola to pay $180 million for 10% of De Beers, Endiama CEO says
stories.summary: Angola will pay about $180 million for a 10 percent stake in De Beers, state diamond miner Endiama's CEO José Manuel Augusto Ganga Júnior said on Friday, joining Namibia and Botswana, already a 15 percent shareholder, among the diamond giant's new owners. He was speaking after Endiama commissioned Angola's first gold refinery in Luanda, able to process 25 kilograms a day, and said the De Beers stake still made sense despite slumping gem prices.

stories.headline: Retailer Mr Price's NKD deal boosts sales, but higher finance costs weigh on profit
stories.summary: South African retailer Mr Price reported a 2.2 percent rise in half-year earnings on Friday, as finance costs from its acquisition of German discount retailer NKD jumped 145 percent to 1 billion rand and weighed on growth. Group retail sales rose 41.8 percent to 25.3 billion rand with NKD contributing 6.9 billion, while Africa sales grew 3.1 percent to 18.4 billion rand on 101 new stores, and the group declared an interim dividend of 329.5 cents per share.

stories.headline: South African rand near one-year low with coalition talks in focus
stories.summary: The South African rand touched a one-year low in early trade on Friday, trading at 17.56 to the dollar, as uncertainty over coalition talks after local elections combined with a stronger dollar and a hawkish split in Thursday's central bank decision to hold rates. Investors are watching whether the ANC and its partners can deliver stable governance in Johannesburg, with the benchmark 2035 government bond steady at a yield of 8.635 percent.

stories.headline: South Africa make lock change for Ireland match
stories.summary: South Africa have been forced into a second-row change for Saturday's Nations Championship clash with Ireland in Dublin, with Franco Mostert, earning his 88th cap, replacing Ruan Nortje after Nortje picked up a training niggle. Coach Rassie Erasmus, serving a six-match ban, will not be allowed into the stadium but worked with the team in the build-up, SA Rugby said.

stories.headline: Markram to lead S Africa in second test against Bangladesh as T20, ODI squads named
stories.summary: Aiden Markram will captain South Africa in Monday's second test against Bangladesh at Centurion, with injured captain Temba Bavuma replaced in the squad by Senuran Muthusamy and Tony de Zorzi likely to come into the playing XI. Cricket South Africa also named its ODI squad, captained by Keshav Maharaj with Lungi Ngidi returning from injury, and a Twenty20 squad led by Bjorn Fortuin for the December series against Bangladesh.

stories.headline: Battered Boks and All Black battle for place in Nations Championship final
stories.summary: South Africa and New Zealand, the world's top two rugby teams, both need wins on Saturday to reach the Nations Championship final on November 29 after surprise defeats last weekend, France beating the Springboks 21-19 and Wales ending a 73-year wait to beat the All Blacks. The All Blacks lead the southern standings by one point, so a bonus-point win over England at Twickenham would put them in the final and close the door on South Africa, who face Ireland in Dublin.

stories.headline: High school valedictorians to get Nike shoes after request from Mississippi’s incoming senator
stories.summary: Senator-elect Scott Colom, who will become Mississippi's first Black senator since Reconstruction, has persuaded Nike to give custom Air Force 1 sneakers to high school valedictorians, and Nike expanded his Mississippi request to valedictorians across the United States for the 2026/27 school year. Colom, who wore Air Force 1s on the campaign trail, framed the shoes as an incentive for students to keep up their grades and suggested the design honour Hiram Revels, the first Black member of Congress.

stories.headline: Wits scoops three South African AI Awards
stories.summary: Wits University has won three categories at the inaugural South African AI Awards, announced in Johannesburg on November 13: its spinout AIrSynQ Systems took Best AI Research and Innovation for AI-powered air quality monitoring, Professor Benjamin Rosman was named AI Talent of the Year, and the Deep Learning Indaba, co-founded by Rosman, Professor Richard Klein and Dr Shakir Mohamed to build a pan-African AI community, won Best Use of AI in Youth Empowerment.

stories.headline: HBCU-style Denver high school Robert F. Smith STEAM Academy to close after split board vote
stories.summary: Denver's school board has voted 4-2 to close the Robert F. Smith STEAM Academy at the end of the school year, the HBCU-modeled high school founded by Black parents and coaches in 2021 that now enrolls just 24 students. Board members who voted no sought a pause over teacher concessions, but Superintendent Alex Marrero said the district was done negotiating and that per-pupil funding made the school financially unsustainable.

stories.headline: Stephen A. Smith Brings HBCU Basketball to BET
stories.summary: Stephen A. Smith's Straight Shooter Media is teaming up with Skydance's BET to telecast HBCU basketball, Variety reported on November 19, in a partnership Smith is building with Entertainment Tonight co-host Kevin Frazier. Smith, a Winston-Salem State alumnus and former HBCU player, has framed the venture as job creation for Black talent and producers as well as games, with Howard's schedule listing six BET broadcasts starting December 3 against Grambling State.

stories.headline: National Digital Literacy Strategy Set To Be Launched
stories.summary: Barbados will launch DigiForward, its national digital literacy initiative from the Ministry of Technological and Vocational Training, on Friday, November 20, aiming to close the country's digital skills gap with a whole-of-society approach. The programme targets small businesses, hospitality workers, seniors, job seekers and people pursuing technical careers such as coding and artificial intelligence, upskilling the current workforce while empowering the general public.

stories.headline: CONDOLENCE MESSAGE | Passing of Ambassador Nigel Barrow
stories.summary: CARICOM has mourned Ambassador Nigel Ainsley Barrow of Barbados, calling him a distinguished public servant and a dedicated proponent of regional integration. As chair of the Inter-Governmental Task Force whose work produced the Revised Treaty of Chaguaramas, Barrow laid the legal foundation for the CARICOM Single Market and Economy, and CARICOM extended condolences to his family, colleagues and friends, and to the Government and people of Barbados.

stories.headline: Alabama’s 14 HBCUs to receive top civil rights honor named for iconic Birmingham activist
stories.summary: For the first time in 24 years, the Birmingham Civil Rights Institute's highest honour will go not to an individual but to all 14 of Alabama's HBCUs, which will collectively receive the 2026 Fred L. Shuttlesworth Human Rights Award. BCRI president and CEO Deborah Bowie said the institutions embody Shuttlesworth's values of dignity and challenging injustice, and they will be recognised at the institute's 34th anniversary celebration on December 1.

stories.headline: NC Central Trains Doulas to Support Black Mothers in Rural North Carolina
stories.summary: North Carolina Central University's Community-Based Birth Doula Training Program, launched in December 2025 through its Rural Health Hub in Enfield, recruits women from rural northeastern counties to support mothers in their own communities.
