The work responds to stark disparities: Black women in North Carolina were 1.7 times as likely as white women to die from pregnancy-related causes from 2018 to 2021, and a state review judged nearly nine in 10 such deaths preventable.

stories.source: The Journal of Blacks in Higher Education
stories.headline: Five African Americans Named Rhodes Scholars
stories.summary: Five of the 32 American Rhodes Scholars announced by the Rhodes Trust are African Americans: MIT senior Arianna G. Doss, Yale senior Richard O. George, George Washington senior Bryson A. Handy, Princeton senior Mya M. Koffie, and Prairie View A&M senior Kailynn M. Weaver, the first Rhodes Scholar from that HBCU. The five will join a cohort of just over 100 scholars worldwide for graduate study at Oxford, with scholarships covering all expenses for two or three years.

stories.headline: Black Women’s Roundtable Unveils Its First 100 Days Federal Policy Agenda Priorities & Congratulates Congressman Hakeem Jeffries on Historic House Speaker Nomination
stories.summary: Following the House Democratic Caucus's nomination of Hakeem Jeffries for speaker, the Black Women's Roundtable has released seven priorities for the first 100 days of the 120th Congress, covering the social safety net, cost of living, health care, jobs and wages, voting rights, gun violence, and combating racism. The priorities, led by NCBCP president and CEO Melanie L. Campbell and informed by a poll of 1,000 registered Black women voters, urge Congress to turn representation into results when it convenes in January 2027.

stories.headline: Terrance Hedgepeth Helps Small Businesses Get AI-Ready
stories.summary: Technology entrepreneur Terrance Hedgepeth is helping small and midsize businesses prepare for artificial intelligence through Designer Technologies, the IT consulting company he founded in 2017 and resumed full-time in 2026, with a focus on cybersecurity, network infrastructure and AI readiness. Black Enterprise, citing AfroTech, notes the work is especially significant for Black-owned and other minority-owned businesses without dedicated technology teams, and Hedgepeth stresses building a reliable foundation before investing in AI, offering a complimentary readiness assessment.

stories.headline: With foreign aid slashed, Africa must 'own its own future', billionaire Ibrahim says
stories.summary: British-Sudanese billionaire Mo Ibrahim has told Reuters that African governments should treat the slump in foreign aid as a chance to own their own future, by closing tax loopholes, tackling capital flight and investing more domestic resources in services such as health and education. His foundation's 2026 governance index found a slight improvement in overall governance over the past decade despite deteriorating security and rule of law, while global aid plunged 23.1 percent in 2025 and Africa loses an estimated $90 billion a year through capital flight.

stories.headline: Nigeria's Tinubu asks parliament to decriminalise attempted suicide
stories.summary: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu has asked parliament to decriminalise attempted suicide and provide support for survivors, treating suicide attempts as a mental health issue rather than a criminal offence. Attempted suicide is currently punishable by a fine, up to a year in jail, or both under Nigeria's criminal and penal codes; the bill would require rehabilitation services and wider access to mental health care if passed.

stories.headline: South Africa central bank maintains policy rate in close call
stories.summary: South Africa's central bank kept its key policy rate unchanged at 7.25 percent on Thursday in a close call, with four Monetary Policy Committee members voting to hold and three favouring a 25-basis-point increase. Governor Lesetja Kganyago said policy was tight enough after two hikes this year, even as inflation rose to 5.2 percent year on year last month, its highest in about two and a half years and above the bank's 3 percent target.

stories.headline: South Africa's ANC and partners near coalition deal to sideline poll-topping DA in Johannesburg
stories.summary: The African National Congress and smaller rivals are closing in on a coalition deal to govern Johannesburg, sidelining the Democratic Alliance despite the DA's first-place finish in this month's local elections with 35 percent of the vote, ahead of the ANC at 20 percent and ActionSA at 16 percent. The potential coalition, covering Gauteng province, would include the ANC, ActionSA, the Economic Freedom Fighters and uMkhonto weSizwe, with final meetings set for Friday, an ANC spokesperson said.

stories.headline: South Africa captain Bavuma to miss second test with calf injury
stories.summary: South Africa captain Temba Bavuma has been ruled out of the second test against Bangladesh with a calf injury he sustained batting in the first test, and will miss Monday's match at Centurion as he begins rehabilitation. Bavuma praised his side's ruthlessness in their nine-wicket win at the Wanderers on Thursday, and said it was too early to say whether he will be ready for the one-day internationals against Bangladesh.

stories.headline: South Africa seal nine-wicket win over Bangladesh in first test
stories.summary: South Africa wrapped up a nine-wicket victory over Bangladesh in the first test at the Wanderers on Thursday to lead the two-match series and stay on course for the World Test Championship final in London next year. Needing just 12 runs after dismissing Bangladesh for 168 in their second innings, with Simon Harmer taking six wickets and Kagiso Rabada three, South Africa have now won 16 of their last 18 tests and sit top of the test rankings.

stories.headline: Kenya chooses US consortium to develop Mrima Hill critical minerals project
stories.summary: Kenya has chosen the Frontier Minerals consortium, which includes American rare earths startup ReElement Technologies and U.S.-based Bunker Hill Silver Corp, to develop the Mrima Hill critical minerals deposit in southeastern Kenya. The mining ministry says preliminary indicators suggest tens of billions of dollars' worth of rare earth minerals plus niobium at the site, a key U.S. target for minerals used in defence and electronics; the winner must now engage the local community and obtain prospecting licences.

stories.headline: Dozens missing as migrant boat capsizes off Senegal coast, NGO says
stories.summary: Dozens of people were missing on Thursday after a boat carrying migrants bound for Europe capsized off Yenne, south of Dakar, according to local NGO Action for Human Rights and Friendship, whose president Adama Mbengue said a survivor reported about 50 people aboard. The sinking is the latest on the dangerous West Africa route, where the UN refugee agency says nearly 8,200 migrants reached the Canary Islands in the first 12 days of November and nearly 600 people have been reported dead or missing in 2026.

stories.headline: Senegal president implements 2026 budget changes by decree amid impasse with parliament
stories.summary: Senegal's President Bassirou Diomaye Faye will implement the revised 2026 budget by decree, his office said on Thursday, as an impasse with parliament threatens a new International Monetary Fund support programme. The standoff stems from a dispute between Faye and his former prime minister Ousmane Sonko, now head of the National Assembly, whose Pastef party controls the assembly and opposes both the revised 2026 budget, rejected on November 3, and the 2027 budget bill voted against on Wednesday.

stories.headline: A'ja Wilson donates pairs of A'Two's to this HBCU hoops program
stories.summary: Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson has surprised Tennessee State University's women's basketball team with customized pairs of her signature Nike A'Two sneakers, which the Lady Tigers personalised through Nike By You. The gift, captured in a video shared by Just Women's Hoops, extends Wilson's support for HBCU programs after she gave her A'One shoes to Benedict College, her father's alma mater, in January.

stories.headline: MP Brown Burke suspended from Parliament for six sittings, after late-night motion approved
stories.summary: Jamaica's Opposition MP Dr Angela Brown Burke has been suspended from the House of Representatives for six sittings after a late-night motion by Leader of Government Business Floyd Green was approved just before midnight. The motion accused the South West St Andrew MP of inappropriate conduct in the chamber, including standing in the aisle and obstructing Speaker Juliet Holness, allegations Brown Burke defended herself against as Opposition MPs challenged the motion's fairness.

stories.headline: Jeffries is One Vote Away From History. Now Comes the Hard Part.
stories.summary: Hakeem Jeffries won the Democratic nomination for House speaker on Wednesday with 251 votes against 11 opponents in a closed-door caucus ballot, putting the Brooklyn representative one formal House vote away from becoming the first Black American to lead the House when the new Congress convenes on January 3. Word In Black reports that Jeffries, 56, must now hold together a caucus split between progressives demanding wholesale change and centrists focused on affordability and health care, while Congressional Black Caucus and NAACP voices press for results beyond the symbolism.

stories.headline: Kickstarter CEO Everette Taylor Named Endowed Chair At Howard University
stories.summary: Kickstarter CEO Everette Taylor has been appointed the John H. Johnson Endowed Chair and Professor of Entrepreneurship at Howard University, effective January 4, 2027, in the Cathy Hughes School of Communications. Announced November 17, the role will have Taylor, Kickstarter's CEO since 2022, lead three to six workshops a year, build a lecture series and advise students through Howard's Innovation Hub, honouring Johnson Publishing founder John H. Johnson.

stories.headline: Lisa Osborne Ross to Become the Next President and CEO of The Executive Leadership Council
stories.summary: The Executive Leadership Council has named Lisa Osborne Ross, former U.S. CEO of Edelman, as its next president and CEO effective January 15, 2027, succeeding Michael C. Hyter, who has led the organisation since March 2021. Ross, an ELC member with more than 30 years across corporate, government and nonprofit leadership, takes over as the preeminent organisation for advancing Black executives in global business marks its 40th anniversary.

stories.headline: Cam Sturdifen Invited to Play in 2027 Allstate HBCU Legacy Bowl
stories.summary: Hampton University safety Cam Sturdifen has been invited to play in the 2027 Allstate HBCU Legacy Bowl, scheduled for February 27, 2027 at Center Parc Stadium in Atlanta and broadcast on NFL Network. The fifth-year standout from Richmond leads the Pirates with 90 tackles, including 56 solo stops, plus three interceptions, two forced fumbles and two recoveries, and will start his 24th consecutive game when Hampton closes the season at Stony Brook on Saturday.

stories.headline: Jeffries endorses lowering Medicare age, adding benefits and universal coverage for kids
stories.summary: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, the favourite to become speaker on January 3, said on Tuesday that Democrats should use their new House and Senate majorities to lower the Medicare eligibility age, add dental, vision and hearing benefits, and provide universal health coverage for children. The agenda goes beyond his pre-election plan to undo Medicaid cuts and restore Affordable Care Act tax credits, and Senator Bernie Sanders said it essentially matches the first year of his Medicare for All proposal, including an eligibility age of 55.

stories.headline: HBCU Grad Expands Opportunities For Young Athletes
stories.summary: Lincoln University graduate and former professional basketball player Antonio DePina founded Scoutz in 2024 to connect high school athletes with college coaches and professional teams, combining AI matching with evaluations from experienced scouts. The platform supports about 15,000 athletes, says 400 have advanced to college or professional competition across 15 countries, and has just raised $600,000 in pre-seed funding led by Delaware Seed, taking its total funding to $1 million as it plans to expand from basketball into volleyball, soccer and football.

stories.headline: Tuskegee University Opens the Center for Genomics and Health Disparity Research
stories.summary: Tuskegee University has opened its new Center for Genomics and Health Disparity Research, a 9,600-square-foot facility with molecular and genomics laboratories, research and office space, and computational infrastructure for data analysis. Scientists at the Alabama HBCU will use computational biology, bioinformatics and AI tools to study diseases that disproportionately affect underserved populations and to train the next generation of researchers, dean Channa Prakash said.

stories.headline: Dr. Helen Fischle Brings a Global Perspective and Innovative Technology to Social Work Education
stories.summary: Alabama A&M University social work professor Dr Helen Fischle, who grew up in Reading, England, to Jamaican parents and studied at Oakwood University, has been selected to serve on the Council on Social Work Education's inaugural Advisory Board on AI and Technology. Fischle coordinates AAMU's Bachelor of Social Work program and its child welfare simulation lab, which uses AI, virtual reality and mixed reality to train students, and the board will guide how emerging technologies are incorporated into social work education and research.

stories.headline: SC State counseling student awarded $9,000 HBCU scholarship
stories.summary: South Carolina State University graduate student Desia Ryant, an Orangeburg native pursuing a Master of Education in counselor education, has received a $9,000 scholarship through the HBCU LEAP Mentoring Program for 2026-27. The Pre-Career Footsteps Mentoring Corps award, housed in the HBCU Center for Excellence in Behavioral Health at Clark Atlanta University, recognises students preparing for careers in behavioral health and counseling, and Ryant, also a seventh-grade teacher, will give behavioral health presentations and work with a mentor during the year.

stories.headline: From College Dreams to Real Opportunities: Mettle Entertainment & Fixing Fathers, Inc., Takes Students to HBCU College Fair in NYC
stories.summary: Connecticut students travelled to New York City for the Malcolm Bernard HBCU College Fair on a trip organised by Fixing Fathers, Inc. and Mettle Entertainment Group, and several returned with scholarship offers and on-the-spot college admissions. The students also received information on financial aid, academic programs and campus life, and the organisers gave away more than $200 in cash prizes during the journey.

stories.headline: Historic Census Undercount of Black Americans Robs Communities of Billions in Funding and Fair Political Representation
stories.summary: The National Urban League is calling for congressional hearings after warning that the 2020 Census undercount of Black Americans could cost Black communities billions of dollars in federal funding and the equivalent of almost three House seats. President and CEO Marc H. Morial said an independent analysis found about 2 million Black Americans went uncounted, with the undercount of Black children up to ten times worse than in 2010, affecting the distribution of about $1.5 trillion across 316 federal programs over the decade.

stories.headline: South Africa inflation accelerates to 5.2% y/y in October, as expected
stories.summary: South Africa's headline consumer inflation rose to 5.2 percent year on year in October from 4.5 percent in September, in line with economists' forecasts, after a sharp increase in domestic petrol and diesel prices. Month on month, inflation was 0.7 percent, up from 0.4 percent in September, with the statistics agency's data underlining the country's exposure to global energy prices because it imports most of its fuel.

stories.headline: Uganda plans to reach financial close of $2.97 billion rail project in Jan 2027
stories.summary: Uganda expects to reach financial close in January 2027 on its €2.70 billion ($2.97 billion) Standard Gauge Railway, Works and Transport Minister Fred Byamukama told lawmakers on Tuesday. The 272-kilometre line, to be built by Turkey's Yapi Merkezi under a 2024 contract, will connect landlocked Uganda to Kenya's railway to the port of Mombasa, and the government also plans early work on a further 1,425 kilometres of extensions toward South Sudan, DR Congo and Rwanda, with the Islamic Development Bank having approved €650.75 million.

stories.headline: Ethiopia and Eritrea amass forces along border, heightening war fears, sources say
stories.summary: Ethiopia and Eritrea have massed forces along their shared border, according to conflict monitors ACLED and the International Crisis Group and sources tied to Tigray militias, raising fears of a direct war between the former rivals. ACLED reported artillery exchanges and clashes near Badme since last week as Ethiopia's army moved against Tigrayan rebels near the border, though a pro-government militia source disputed that the two armies had clashed, and Eritrea's information minister dismissed Ethiopian claims as propaganda.

stories.headline: South Africa to probe treatment of Olympic champion Smith after her defection
stories.summary: South Africa's sports minister Gayton McKenzie has ordered an inquiry into the treatment of Olympic swimming champion Tatjana Smith, the country's most decorated Olympian with four medals, after she announced she will represent the Netherlands in future. McKenzie apologised to Smith, whose $35,000 in 2023 World Championships prize money was withheld for 12 months, and asked the South African Sports Confederation and Olympic Committee to investigate Swimming South Africa.

stories.headline: Falcon 6X: Why Ghana is facing backlash over new $60m presidential jet
stories.summary: Ghana's government has defended taking delivery of a new $60 million French-made Dassault Falcon 6X presidential jet, delivered to the Ghana Air Force on Monday, amid opposition and public criticism over its cost during a cost-of-living squeeze. Parliament approved the purchase last December as part of a military aviation modernisation that also includes four Airbus helicopters; ministers say an improving economy makes it affordable and that it replaces a 16-year-old Falcon 900EX with recurring maintenance problems, while opposition MP Samuel Abu Jinapor questioned the government's priorities and consistency.

stories.headline: Two Southern University esports players advance to national title games
stories.summary: Southern University esports players Jaeveon Jordan and Issac Williamson have swept their semifinal opponents to reach the PlayVS College League Fall National Championship Finals in College Football 27, Jordan in Division I and Williamson in Division II. Coach Christopher Turner, director of SU EDGE, called having finalists in both divisions a monumental achievement for HBCU esports, noting research showing Black student-athletes are just 1.3 percent of collegiate esports competitors nationwide; the finals are scheduled for the week of November 30.

stories.headline: Morehouse and Spelman's sibling exchange forges lasting bonds between freshmen men and women
stories.summary: For more than 40 years, Morehouse College and Spelman College's annual sibling exchange has paired incoming freshmen across the two Atlanta HBCUs, a SpelHouse tradition organised by the schools' student government associations and orientation leaders. Students and alumni say the pairings, made as freshmen line up and cross paths in Morehouse's King Chapel, often become lifelong bonds and support networks that carry through college and into professional life.

stories.headline: Atletico Madrid forward Lookman out with high-grade knee sprain
stories.summary: Atletico Madrid forward Ademola Lookman suffered a high-grade knee sprain while on international duty with Nigeria, the LaLiga club said on Tuesday, with no recovery timeline given. Nigeria's medical staff had initially called the injury a minor sprain sustained during the Super Eagles' 3-1 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying win over Tanzania on Friday; the 29-year-old, who joined Atletico from Atalanta in February, will undergo physiotherapy and rehabilitation.

stories.headline: Nigeria arrests eight in cocaine gang routing drugs to Europe via Sahara
stories.summary: Nigeria's National Drug Law Enforcement Agency says it has dismantled a transnational syndicate that smuggled cocaine from Lagos through Kano and across the Sahara via Niger and Libya to Europe, arresting eight suspected couriers. The suspects, arrested in Lagos and Kano in late October, excreted a total of 634 pellets weighing 13.795 kilograms in custody and told investigators they planned to travel by road to Europe, the agency said.

stories.headline: AngloGold Ashanti to invest about $2.5 billion in Colombia copper mine
stories.summary: South African miner AngloGold Ashanti plans to invest about $2.5 billion in the Quebradona copper project in Colombia's Antioquia department, conditional on environmental permits, corporate affairs manager Stewart Bailey said at a government event in New York on Tuesday. The mine is expected to produce 80,000 metric tons a year and generate about $1.5 billion a year in exports, with construction due to begin in 2028 once permits are obtained.

stories.headline: All 36 States Approve State Police Bill
stories.summary: All 36 Nigerian state Houses of Assembly have approved a constitutional amendment to create state police services alongside a federal police service, Clerk to the National Assembly Kamoru Ogunlana announced on Monday, clearing the way for the bill to go to President Bola Tinubu for assent. The unanimous backing exceeds the 24 states required for a constitutional amendment; states would then need their own laws, funding and recruitment before any state force could operate.

stories.headline: Retired EY executive to lead Raleigh HBCU’s reorganization
stories.summary: Saint Augustine's University in Raleigh has a new chief restructuring officer: the historically Black university's board voted on November 7 to ask the bankruptcy court to appoint retired EY executive Coley, a former SAU professor who lives in Charlotte, and Judge David Warren granted the appointment on November 10 along with an extension to January 8, 2027 to file a reorganization plan. Coley will lead the Chapter 11 restructuring with decision-making authority as the university, whose accreditation was revoked in 2025 over financial and management concerns, assesses exit financing, investment and partnership options ahead of its next hearing on January 11, 2027.

stories.headline: Fayetteville State Band Holds No. 1 D-II HBCU Ranking Ahead of National Band Competition
stories.summary: Fayetteville State University's Marching Bronco Xpress sits atop the Division II HBCU band rankings as it bids to return to the Red Lobster ESPN Band of the Year National Competition in Atlanta, where it was a national finalist last year. The band, which has grown from 40 members in 2021 to 140 under director of bands Austin Chalmers, earned the No. 1 ranking in October, and the coming final top-10 rankings will decide which band represents the East Division at the national championship.

stories.headline: University of Maryland, Eastern Shore backers sue for 136 years of underfunding
stories.summary: Supporters of the University of Maryland, Eastern Shore, grouped as ForUMES and including students, faculty, alumni and prospective applicants, are suing the state in federal court for billions of dollars in relief, claiming Maryland has deliberately underfunded the Princess Anne HBCU since it became a land-grant institution in 1890. The complaint, filed October 26, names Governor Wes Moore and state higher education officials; the university itself says it has great relations with the state, which notes record HBCU funding and recent support including nearly $15 million toward the campus's new School of Veterinary Medicine, the first at a public HBCU in the nation.

stories.headline: The Five Surprising Pieces of Black History Found in the Closets of HBCU Radio Stations
stories.summary: The Mellon-funded HBCU Radio Preservation Project, led by Jocelyn Robinson, is rescuing endangered recordings from HBCU radio stations before aging reels and cassettes are lost, HBCU News reports. Its finds include Fisk University's first-ever broadcast, more than 65 hours of campus life digitized at Elizabeth City State's WRVS, and Central State's WCSU community reaction to Toni Morrison's death; a four-year, $5 million Mellon grant announced in 2024 through WYSO is expanding the preservation work across 29 HBCU radio stations.

stories.headline: Tim O'Neal talks diversity, longevity on PGA Tour Champions
stories.summary: Jackson State product Tim O'Neal, 54, was the lone Black golfer among the 36 qualifiers at the PGA Tour Champions season finale, the Charles Schwab Cup Championship in Phoenix from November 12 to 15, his third straight appearance there in a pro career approaching 30 years. O'Neal, who posted five top-10 finishes in 27 events in 2026, told the Arizona Republic that the roughly $100,000-a-year cost of developing as a pro remains a barrier for Black and HBCU golfers, pointing to supports such as the PGA Tour's HBCU Golf Impact Grant, which pledges $250,000 to 10 partner schools and 16 golf programs.

stories.headline: AACUC Announces 2027 African American Credit Union Hall of Fame Honorees
stories.summary: The African-American Credit Union Coalition will induct four leaders into the African American Credit Union Hall of Fame on March 2, 2027 at the Hamilton Hotel in Washington, DC, during the Governmental Affairs Conference: BECU Foundation executive director Gloria Dixon, who oversees more than $8 million a year in nonprofit giving, NASCUS president and CEO Brian Knight, 40 Groups founder Dennis Sullivan, and Verity Credit Union president and CEO Tonita Webb, the first Black woman to lead that organisation, whose doctoral research focused on credit union strategies for reducing the wealth gap.

stories.headline: Aramark Collegiate Hospitality Selected as N.C. A&T Dining Partner
stories.summary: Aramark Collegiate Hospitality has been selected as the long-term dining services provider for North Carolina A&T State University, the nation's largest public HBCU, beginning January 1, 2027, in a partnership branded the N.C. A&T Culinary Collective. The agreement, won after a competitive review at a university serving more than 15,000 students and pursuing Research 1 status, covers a renovation of Williams Dining Hall and other venues, ten paid student internships across marketing, culinary and human resources, digital ordering platforms, and menus sourced from the university's College of Agriculture and Environmental Sciences and local farmers.

stories.headline: Dangote Refinery to expand IPO by up to 30% to $2.1 billion, sources say
stories.summary: Nigeria's Dangote Refinery plans to enlarge its initial public offering by up to 30 percent to about $2.1 billion after orders reached nearly 6 trillion naira, about $4.5 billion and roughly three times the shares initially on offer, Reuters reports. The refinery, built by Aliko Dangote, is now expected to allot up to 5.33 billion shares including an overallotment option and to list in Nigeria later this month, with retail investors and local pension funds receiving close to their full requests while overseas allocations are scaled back, and Dangote expected to retain about 83.5 percent afterward.

stories.headline: Telkom profit rises on mobile, fibre growth
stories.summary: South African telecommunications group Telkom said its half-year headline earnings rose 9.3 percent, with headline earnings per share up to 334.1 cents in the six months to September 30 from 305.6 cents a year earlier, helped by mobile and fibre data growth. Group revenue rose 2 percent to 22.5 billion rand as data revenue grew 6.6 percent to 13.9 billion rand, now 61.8 percent of the total, Openserve fibre revenue rose 4.2 percent with the fibre connectivity rate improving to 54.8 percent, and the group, which is majority government-owned, said it is in early takeover talks with bigger rival MTN.

stories.headline: Wyclef Jean on Why the Grammys Still Matter to Reggae and Dancehall: ‘Bob Marley Never Got a Grammy in His Life’
stories.summary: Haitian-born, three-time Grammy winner Wyclef Jean told World Music Views at Kingston's Spanish Court Hotel, on the day the 2027 Grammy nominations were announced, that the awards still matter for reggae and dancehall because they bring visibility and national pride to artists from small island nations. Jean noted that Bob Marley never won a competitive Grammy in his lifetime, though he received a Lifetime Achievement Award in 2001, and recalled carrying the Haitian flag on stage when he won, as Stephen Marley did with the Jamaican flag, before an audience of more than 24 million.

stories.headline: Ghana Sends a Record 13,268 Students to the United States as Nigeria Falls to 20,634
stories.summary: Ghana sent a record 13,268 students to the United States in the 2025/26 academic year, up 3.5 percent, according to the Open Doors 2026 count reported by Today News Africa. Nigeria's total fell 5.6 percent from its own record to 20,634 students over the same period.

stories.headline: 21 HBCUs Form National Research Alliance at UVI Summit on St. Thomas
stories.summary: Representatives of 21 HBCUs have agreed to form the HBCU RISE Alliance, a national research alliance to share resources, coordinate federal funding proposals and expand opportunities for students and faculty, following a November 10-11 summit hosted by the University of the Virgin Islands on St. Thomas and convened by the Thurgood Marshall College Fund's Payne Research Center. Summit data showed HBCUs are 3 percent of U.S. colleges but award 25 percent of STEM bachelor's degrees earned by Black students, while submitting less than 2 percent of National Science Foundation proposals, and a new alignment report found 582 of 1,322 faculty research profiles matching federal priorities in fields including agriculture, health, advanced materials and artificial intelligence.

stories.headline: Amputee Football World Cup:: Black Challenge storm into Round of 16 with emphatic 6-0 rout of Iraq
stories.summary: Ghana's Black Challenge amputee football team thrashed Iraq 6-0 on Monday in their final Group D match at Lucia II in San Juan de los Lagos to reach the round of 16 at the 2026 WAFF Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico. The two-time African champions, coached by Stephen Richard Obeng, finished second in the group behind Angola's seven points after recovering from a 2-0 opening defeat to Angola and a 1-1 draw with Colombia on Sunday.

stories.headline: WHO Validates Eritrea's Elimination of Trachoma as a Public Health Problem
stories.summary: The World Health Organization has validated Eritrea's elimination of trachoma as a public health problem, the 11th such validation in the WHO African Region and the 34th worldwide, Today News Africa reports. The milestone follows two decades of work under the SAFE strategy across all 58 of the country's sub-zobas.

stories.headline: Jose Maria Neves Wins a Second Term as President of Cape Verde as Joana Rosa Concedes Defeat
stories.summary: Cape Verde President Jose Maria Neves has won a second five-year term with 63.8 percent of the vote in provisional results, Today News Africa reports. His opponent Joana Rosa, the first woman to run for the country's presidency, has conceded defeat.

stories.headline: DFC Puts Its Largest-Ever Equity Bet at the Center of Africa Tech Festival Week in South Africa
stories.summary: The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation is taking its largest-ever equity investment, up to $155 million in African connectivity provider WIOCC, into Africa Tech Festival week in Cape Town, Today News Africa reports. The corporation is using the festival to hunt for further deals under a $205 billion mandate.

stories.headline: Delaware State University Certifies Record Fall 2026 Enrollment of 7,407 Students
stories.summary: Delaware State University has certified its fall 2026 enrollment at 7,407 students, the largest in its 135-year history and up 784 students, or 11.8 percent, from last fall's 6,623. Of the total, 5,959 are on the Dover campuses and in online programs, itself a record, with the rest enrolled through international partnerships spanning the Caribbean, Asia and Africa; graduate enrollment rose 27.1 percent, the in-state freshman class is the largest ever, and the Delaware State-led eHBCU online consortium has grown in its first year to include Alabama State, the Southern University System and Pensole Lewis College.

stories.headline: Six HBCU Football Programs Reach 2026 NCAA Division II Playoffs
stories.summary: Six HBCU football programs were selected on Sunday, November 15 for the 32-team NCAA Division II championship, with the SIAC setting a conference record by placing four teams: No. 1 seed Benedict, Kentucky State, Central State and Edward Waters. CIAA champion Virginia Union and at-large pick Fayetteville State complete the six, four of them host first-round games on Saturday, November 21, Central State is making its first playoff appearance since 1986, ending a 40-year drought, and Edward Waters is in the playoffs for the first time.

stories.headline: Southern’s Ckelby Givens on the brink of making SWAC
stories.summary: Southern defensive star Ckelby Givens became the university's all-time career sacks leader on Saturday night, recording two sacks in the Jaguars' 41-28 win over Alcorn State to reach 41 for his career. The second sack broke the school record, and Givens now needs just half a sack to match Michael Strahan's SWAC record of 41.5, set at Texas Southern from 1989 to 1992; he finished with three tackles, two sacks and two tackles for loss as Southern improved to 6-5 in its final home game.

stories.headline: Fort Valley State has fired its head football coach
stories.summary: Fort Valley State University has parted ways with head football coach Marlon Watson, announcing the decision on Friday, November 13 through social media, with the dismissal effective immediately and an interim head coach to be appointed. Watson was hired in February 2025 after serving as linebackers coach at Georgia Military College; the university gave no specific reason and no timetable for a permanent replacement, and the move came the same weekend Bethune-Cookman dismissed Raymond Woodie Jr. and named Alvin “Shine” Wyatt interim coach.

stories.headline: Baltimore Boudoir Photographer Nicole Griffin Wins Boudoir Category in 2026 Best of Baltimore Weddings Readers’ Poll
stories.summary: Nicole Griffin Photography, a Black woman-owned, appointment-only boudoir studio in Baltimore serving Washington, DC, Maryland and Northern Virginia, has been named the Boudoir category winner in the 2026 Best of Baltimore Weddings Readers' Poll, which drew 22,198 votes across 95 categories. Founder Nicole Griffin built the studio around photographing women exactly as they are, and the reader-voted win adds to her Gold and Bronze medals at the Professional Photographers of America International Photographic Competition in 2026.

stories.headline: Nigeria expects six-country African digital trade accord this month, minister says
stories.summary: Nigeria expects to sign an agreement this month with Ghana, Rwanda, Kenya, South Africa and Egypt to make it easier for digital-service companies to expand across their markets, Trade and Investment Minister Jumoke Oduwole told Reuters. The accord is expected to be signed at an African Continental Free Trade Area Council of Ministers meeting in Zimbabwe, following a regulatory roundtable with the six countries' central banks and trade ministries, though Oduwole gave no details on whether it would change licensing, taxation or capital requirements, and the push is aimed particularly at fintech and other digitally enabled services.

stories.headline: UN labour agency chief Houngbo wins second term
stories.summary: Togo's Gilbert Houngbo, the International Labour Organization's first African director-general, won a second five-year term on Monday with 51 of the 56 votes cast, after his two rivals, Spain's Labour Minister Yolanda Diaz and Peru's former foreign minister Javier Gonzalez-Olaechea, withdrew. Reuters notes the ILO faces a financial crisis over United States non-payments that could lead to further job cuts.

stories.headline: South Africa police probe two weekend shootings that left 17 dead
stories.summary: South African police are investigating two weekend shootings that left 17 people dead: nine victims, including three women, were found shot inside a shack in Jeffsville, an informal settlement in Pretoria's Atteridgeville township, in a shooting late on Sunday whose motive has not been established and in which no arrests have been made. Separately, eight people were found shot dead inside a vehicle outside Pietermaritzburg in KwaZulu-Natal on Sunday night, in a country where police note the murder rate averages about 60 a day.

stories.headline: Black Challenge Held By Colombia As Ghana Search For First World Cup Victory
stories.summary: Ghana's Black Challenge amputee football team drew 1-1 with Colombia on Sunday in their second Group D match at the 2026 WAFF Amputee Football World Cup in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico, a 24-team tournament running November 13 to 22. The improved performance under head coach Stephen Richard Obeng followed a 2-0 opening defeat to former champions Angola, and Ghana must now beat Iraq in their final group game on Monday to keep their knockout hopes alive, with the Ghana Amputee Football Association calling on Ghanaians to support the team.

stories.headline: Ramaphosa Urges South Africa to Harness AI Opportunities
stories.summary: President Cyril Ramaphosa used a Monday address in Silicon Valley to urge South Africa to seize the opportunities of the global AI revolution to boost economic growth, create jobs and improve competitiveness, leading a delegation of government officials, business leaders, academics and researchers. He cited a Microsoft AI Economy Institute report ranking South Africa 46th of 147 economies for AI adoption and a Google and Ipsos survey showing South Africans embracing AI above the global average, pointed to data centres, fibre and cloud as investment areas where South Africa already holds Africa's largest share of data centre capacity, and said the country must become a creator and producer of AI, not only a consumer, while protecting jobs and digital sovereignty.

stories.headline: Gov’t approves MOU for creation of AI infrastructure in Jamaica, says Holness
stories.summary: Jamaica's Government has approved a memorandum of understanding with a group of investors to explore establishing artificial intelligence infrastructure in Jamaica, Prime Minister Andrew Holness announced on Sunday at the Jamaica Labour Party's annual conference in Montego Bay. Holness did not say whether the MOU covers AI data centres on the island, but said it means Jamaica can have a footprint in the technology and be part of creating it, not only a consumer of it; the report is sourced from the Jamaica Observer.

stories.headline: US basketball player arrested after cannabis seizure at Nigeria airport, authorities say
stories.summary: Nigeria's National Drug Law Enforcement Agency said it arrested American basketball professional Greene Da'monte Khiree, 28, of Savannah, Georgia, after officers found 33.95 kilograms of cannabis in two suitcases he abandoned at Lagos's Murtala Muhammed International Airport. The agency said he arrived on November 11 on an Emirates flight from Thailand via Dubai, that the bags held 32 parcels of cannabis and a tracking device, and that he was arrested in the airport car park after being kept under surveillance; he told officers he has lived and played professionally in Thailand since October 2025 and had come to Nigeria on holiday.

stories.headline: Floyd Norman Receives Honorary Oscar at 91
stories.summary: Floyd Norman, 91, received an Honorary Oscar on Sunday, November 15 at the Academy's 17th Governors Awards, presented by Mahershala Ali, honouring a career that began in 1956 when he joined Walt Disney Animation Studios as its first Black animator. Norman contributed to Sleeping Beauty, The Sword in the Stone, Mary Poppins and The Jungle Book, later worked on The Hunchback of Notre Dame, Mulan and Pixar's Toy Story 2 and Monsters, Inc., co-founded the Black-owned Vignette Films, which made educational films about Black history, and was named a Disney Legend in 2007.

stories.headline: Georgia’s black voters want more than victory
stories.summary: Black voters powered a Democratic sweep of Georgia's statewide races, including flipping the Public Service Commission, with nearly all the incoming statewide officeholders Black women and Carolyn Hugley of Columbus set to become House speaker, but those voters now expect action on wages, housing and jobs rather than celebration. In Stonecrest, where about six in ten voters turned out and roughly 90 percent backed Democrats, and across the state, organisers such as Georgia STAND-UP's Deborah Scott say years of Black women-led organising delivered the wins, and the test is whether the new government answers the economic complaints behind them.

stories.headline: Nigerian-American, Ohaebosim elected Kansas’ first Black Lt. Gov. in 139 years
stories.summary: Nigerian-American Kelechi “KC” Ohaebosim has been elected lieutenant governor of Kansas alongside Democratic gubernatorial candidate Cindy Holscher, defeating Republicans Ty Masterson and Jeffrey Klemp in the November 3 election, which the Associated Press called on November 12 after a statewide audit confirmed Holscher's lead. Born in Wichita in 1978 to a Nigerian father, Dr Linus Ohaebosim, he becomes Kansas's first Black statewide elected official since Edward McCabe, who served as state auditor from 1883 to 1887.

stories.headline: Black Britain news round-up: African and Caribbean GCSEs, Kelso Cochrane and David Lammy
stories.summary: Black Current News's weekly round-up leads with BLAM UK, founded by Ife Thompson, writing to the Education Secretary to ask the government to back GCSEs in African and Caribbean languages such as Yoruba, Nigerian Pidgin and Jamaican Patois, following a £340,000 funding commitment for a Ukrainian GCSE, and asking exam boards and Ofqual to explain how languages are chosen and to consult African and Caribbean communities. The round-up also reports David Lammy becoming an ambassador for Prostate Cancer Research, backing wider targeted screening for men at higher risk including Black men, and Kelso Cochrane's family calling on the Metropolitan Police to apologise for its investigation of his 1959 murder in North Kensington.

stories.headline: Benedict Stages Historic Second-Half Rally To Win SIAC Championship
stories.summary: Benedict rallied from 38-14 down in the third quarter to beat Kentucky State 52-45 in overtime in Columbia and win the 2026 SIAC Championship, Demetris McKelvey catching a 25-yard touchdown on the first play of overtime before the Tigers held the Thorobreds scoreless on their possession. Benedict, 10-1 and the No. 1 team in Super Region II, earned the SIAC's automatic NCAA Division II playoff bid, while Kentucky State fell to 8-3 and is expected to take an at-large place.

stories.headline: Spelman's Roz Brewer and Tyler Perry Join Georgia Governor-Elect's Transition Team
stories.summary: Spelman College alumna and Fortune 500 executive Roz Brewer and Atlanta entertainment mogul Tyler Perry have been tapped to serve on Georgia Governor-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms' transition team, bringing corporate and creative-industry experience to the planning for the incoming administration. Their roles were not detailed in the report, which frames the appointments as an example of HBCU graduates shaping policy and priorities at the highest levels of state government.

stories.headline: Week 11 HBCU Football Recap: Prairie View Wins as Time Expires, Alabama State Upsets Jackson State, and Both SWAC Races Flip
stories.summary: Week 11 flipped both SWAC races: Ethan Eddins kicked a 43-yard field goal as time expired to give Prairie View A&M a 13-10 win at Arkansas-Pine Bluff and sole possession of the West lead, while Alabama State beat Jackson State 20-13 on an end-zone interception with six seconds left, handing East control to Alabama A&M after its 35-6 win over Texas Southern. Southern, Grambling State, Florida A&M, North Carolina A&T and Tennessee State also won on a Saturday that left both divisions to be settled on November 21.

stories.headline: Michael Olunga looking to break Kenya scoring record against South Africa
stories.summary: Kenya striker Michael Olunga can become his country's outright all-time top scorer if he scores against South Africa on Tuesday, after his goal in Friday's 2-2 AFCON 2027 qualifying draw with Bafana Bafana took him to 35 international goals, equalling William Ouma's record. Harambee Stars coach Benni McCarthy praised the veteran, who has just returned from a long injury layoff, for his pressing and for converting a penalty against goalkeeper Ronwen Williams.

stories.headline: Working Visit: President Ramaphosa arrives in California
stories.summary: President Cyril Ramaphosa arrived in California on Saturday, November 14 to lead a multi-stakeholder South African delegation on a Silicon Valley working visit aimed at strengthening the country's artificial intelligence capabilities and attracting investment. The programme, centred on a South Africa AI Opportunity gathering under the theme Building the African AI Economy, covers frontier AI, robotics, data infrastructure and cloud computing, with the Presidency saying the visit will inform South Africa's approach to developing, adopting and applying the technology.

stories.headline: Dangote Refinery drives Nigeria’s £1bn refined fuel exports to UK
stories.summary: Britain bought £1.02 billion of refined petroleum products from Nigeria in the 12 months to June 2026, more than double the year before and 53.5 percent of all UK goods imports from Nigeria, according to the UK government's latest Trade and Investment Factsheet published on November 6. BusinessDay attributes the shift, in which refined fuel overtook crude oil as Nigeria's leading petroleum export to Britain, to the 650,000-barrel-per-day Dangote Petroleum Refinery in Lagos widening its presence in international fuel markets.

stories.headline: Jamaica Defeats Mexico in Nations League Quarterfinals First Leg
stories.summary: Jamaica beat defending champion Mexico 3-2 at the National Stadium in Kingston on Saturday in the first leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal, scoring three goals against Mexico for the first time in the Reggae Boyz's history. A Jesús Gallardo own goal, Renaldo Cephas's strike just after halftime and Richard King's penalty put Jamaica 3-0 up before late goals from Gilberto Mora and Julián Quiñones cut the deficit, with the second leg set for Tuesday in Monterrey.

stories.headline: Jamaica Bids Farewell to Lieutenant Stitchie, a Pioneer in Dancehall and Gospel
stories.summary: Jamaica said farewell to dancehall and gospel artiste Lieutenant Stitchie at a thanksgiving service in St Andrew on Saturday, November 14, the veteran deejay best known for his 1986 hit Wear Yuh Size having died at Kingston Public Hospital on September 28. A former schoolteacher from Spanish Town's sound-system scene who became a born-again Christian in 1997 and took his delivery into gospel reggae, Stitchie received the Order of Distinction in 2021, and tributes at the Louise Bennett Garden Theatre came from his daughter Johanna Laing, fellow artistes Papa San and Carlene Davis, and Culture Minister Olivia Grange.

stories.headline: Ghana risks political capture by drug cartels if narcotics menace persists – Kutin
stories.summary: Security analyst Emmanuel Kutin warned on Channel One TV's The Big Issue on Saturday that drug trafficking cartels could infiltrate Ghana's political parties and eventually influence who becomes president if the country does not confront the growing narcotics trade, pointing to Guinea-Bissau as the path to avoid. His comments followed Spanish authorities' November 11 seizure of 2.6 tonnes of cocaine concealed in a coconut shipment from Ghana, and he urged parties to treat narcotics as a national security issue, tighten political financing, and avoid labelling Ghana a cocaine economy.

stories.headline: Melissa Sigodo wins Global Majority Impact Award for journalism
stories.summary: Journalist Melissa Sigodo, founder of The Community Reporter, received a Global Majority Impact Award for journalism at the inaugural ceremony in Basildon on Saturday, November 14, recognising a year of reporting on policing, healthcare and Black communities across Britain. Her publication's work included prompting West Midlands Police to reopen an investigation into a racist image reported by Leah-Ruth Daniel, covering the campaign to restore a dedicated sickle cell emergency unit at the Royal London Hospital, and a four-part Windrush compensation series following one couple's five-year fight for redress.

stories.headline: VUU WINS CIAA FOOTBALL CHAMPIONSHIP
stories.summary: Virginia Union beat Johnson C. Smith 15-14 in Durham on Saturday to win the 2026 CIAA Football Championship, game MVP Ramon Brown sprinting 69 yards for the winning touchdown with 12:37 left after Gage Miller's three first-half field goals had kept the Panthers close. The title is Virginia Union's second in three years and its first 10-win season since 1991, and it carries the CIAA's automatic NCAA Division II playoff berth, with the Panthers' opponent to be named in Sunday's selection show.

stories.headline: THREE-PEAT CHAMPIONS! SC State Captures 21st MEAC Football Title With 38-24 Victory Over NC Central
stories.summary: South Carolina State beat North Carolina Central 38-24 in Orangeburg on Saturday to capture its 21st MEAC football championship and its third straight title under head coach Chennis Berry, breaking a 24-24 halftime tie with a 14-point third quarter while holding the Eagles scoreless in the second half. Keely Watson threw three touchdown passes and Malaqhi Jones caught two scores for the Bulldogs, who finished 4-0 in the MEAC at 9-2 overall and earned the conference's berth in the Cricket Celebration Bowl in Atlanta.

stories.headline: Dr. Glenda Baskin Glover Urges Congress to Strengthen Morrill Act Funding for HBCUs
stories.summary: Tennessee State University President Dr Glenda Baskin Glover is pressing Congress to strengthen Morrill Act funding for historically Black land-grant universities, arguing that the dual system created by the Second Morrill Act of 1890 has never reached funding parity with predominantly white peers. Glover, who has led Tennessee State since 2013 and focused on recovering decades of missing state funding, says closing the gap requires deliberate federal action on appropriations, not just individual institutional efforts.

stories.headline: Coco Gauff is youngest player since Maria Sharapova to have 40+ top-10 wins
stories.summary: Coco Gauff's 6-4, 7-5 win over Marta Kostyuk in her WTA Finals group finale made her the youngest player since Maria Sharapova in 2009 to reach 40 career wins over top-10 opponents, OptaAce figures show. Gauff, 22 and ranked No. 4, rallied from 5-1 down in the second set, saving three set points and winning the last six games, but still missed the semifinals despite a 2-1 group record after Jessica Pegula beat Linda Noskova.

stories.headline: CIAA Friday Night Blitz: Fayetteville State Overcomes 21-Point Deficit, Defeats Virginia State
stories.summary: Fayetteville State erased a 21-point deficit to beat Virginia State 31-29 in the CIAA's inaugural Friday Night Blitz at Durham County Memorial Stadium, John Hernandez-Vargas kicking the winning 30-yard field goal with 1:47 left before Virginia State missed a 29-yarder as time expired. The Broncos, now 8-3 with six straight wins, outgained the Trojans 406-370 and strengthened their NCAA Division II playoff case, while Virginia State fell to 7-4 with a third straight loss.

stories.headline: New NAACP Report Warns AI Could Deepen Health Disparities in Black Communities
stories.summary: A new NAACP and Sanofi report, AI Fluency is a Challenge on Both Sides of the Exam Room, released at AfroTech 2026 as the third ACE Your Health StoryMap, warns that healthcare deserts, broadband gaps and distrust could stop Black Americans benefiting from AI in medicine. Drawing on input from nearly 23,000 community members, it notes that one in three Americans lives in a healthcare desert, about 3.8 million Black Americans lack a home broadband subscription, and nearly two-thirds of Black adults see racial bias as a major problem in healthcare.

stories.headline: NEW YORK CITY LANDMARKS SHINE PINK AND BLUE AS JACK AND JILL CELEBRATES THE NEXT GENERATION OF BLACK LEADERS
stories.summary: Four New York City buildings, including One World Trade Center, were to light up in pink and blue on November 13-14 as Jack and Jill of America marked its Eastern Region Metropolitan Cluster Area Work Day under the theme Empowered Women, Empowering Generations. Nearly 1,000 mothers, youth and leaders were expected for the two-day gathering, whose Metropolitan Chapter, founded in 1939, has awarded 24 four-year college scholarships since 2020 and provides winter essentials to about 800 New Yorkers a year.

stories.headline: AFCON qualifiers: Salah scores twice as Egypt hit Malawi for five; Libya stun Tunisia and Kenya hold South Africa
stories.summary: Mohamed Salah scored twice as Egypt beat Malawi 5-0 in Cairo in the AFCON 2027 qualifiers, while Libya stunned Tunisia 2-0, Morocco thrashed Niger 5-1 and Nigeria beat Tanzania 3-1 in Uyo. Kenya held South Africa 2-2 through Ryan Ogam's stoppage-time equaliser, and Ghana won an AFCON qualifier for the first time since November 2023, beating Somalia 2-0, with the return games set for Tuesday.

stories.headline: Dangote in Talks with Ghana Over 500,000-Tonne Cocoa Processing Deal
stories.summary: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote is in talks with Ghana over a proposed deal to process 500,000 metric tonnes of cocoa locally, Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson told Joy News, saying Dangote had contacted him and President John Dramani Mahama directly. No terms have been finalised or signed, and the proposal would support Ghana's target of processing at least 50 percent of its cocoa domestically by 2028 and 100 percent by 2030.

stories.headline: Young African innovators develop digital tools to track blood supplies,predict shortages
stories.summary: Young innovators from five African countries showcased digital tools to track blood supplies and predict shortages at the Terumo BCT Africa Hackathon 2026 at Strathmore University in Nairobi on November 13. Team Relay, of Kenyan and Nigerian innovators, won the $5,000 top prize for HemoGrid, which helps hospitals find available blood stocks and coordinate transfers, while Kenya's Medibora was second with Providus, a forecasting system usable by dashboard, USSD and SMS, though the prototypes are not yet ready for nationwide use.

stories.headline: Proteas unveil playing XI for opening Bangladesh Test
stories.summary: South Africa have named their playing XI for the first World Test Championship Test against Bangladesh, starting Sunday in Johannesburg, making two changes to the side that beat Australia. Zubayr Hamza returns at No. 3 for the first time since February 2024 and Dane Paterson joins a pace attack led by Kagiso Rabada, while captain Temba Bavuma leads a side now top of the Test rankings, with the second Test in Centurion from November 23.

stories.headline: Ruto, Cabinet Secretaries Make Fresh Government Appointments
stories.summary: President William Ruto and several Cabinet Secretaries have made a fresh round of appointments and reappointments to Kenyan government institutions and state agencies in a Gazette Notice dated November 13, 2026. Ruto appointed Dr Geoffrey Odundo as Chancellor of Machakos University for five years, while other appointments covered bodies including the Kenya Institute for Public Policy Research and Analysis, the Private Security Regulatory Authority and the Kenya Forest Service, mostly for three-year terms.

stories.headline: South African court clears Phala Phala committee to choose a new evidence leader
stories.summary: The Western Cape High Court has dismissed two applications challenging Parliament's withdrawal of advocate Thandazani Madonsela SC as chief evidence leader for the Section 89 inquiry into President Cyril Ramaphosa, leaving the committee free to choose another appointment. The November 13 judgment, which made no costs order, addressed only the appointment process and not the underlying Phala Phala allegations, and committee chair Makashule Gana says the committee will meet next week to consider a new evidence leader.

stories.headline: AfroTech's Growth Shows the Power of Black Tech Talent
stories.summary: Inc. traces AfroTech's growth from a planned 400-person San Francisco gathering in 2016, which drew more than 650, to last week's 10th anniversary conference in Houston, which brought together more than 35,000 people and over 300 speakers. Blavity founder Morgan DeBaun told the magazine the conference, newsroom, recruiting platform and year-round AfroTech Insider membership were each built by starting over as the work evolved, with this year's edition emphasising hands-on AI learning and a new HealthStack programme for clinicians.

stories.headline: Microsoft 365 Outage: What Campuses Should Know
stories.summary: A Microsoft 365 outage that began on Thursday, November 12 entered a second day on Friday, disrupting Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other services worldwide, with Reuters reporting 138,058 Downdetector reports at the peak and Microsoft linking the problem to infrastructure supporting Exchange Online while reporting improving availability. HBCU News notes Microsoft's incident notices listed Microsoft 365 Education services as potentially affected, while establishing no outage at any specific HBCU, and frames the episode as a prompt for campuses to review backup communication plans for financial aid, faculty and student-services messages.

stories.headline: Kenya's Farmerlifeline wins $50K Smart Africa AI farming grant
stories.summary: Kenya-based Farmerlifeline Technologies has won the third edition of Smart Africa's Innovate Africa Challenge, securing a $50,000 implementation grant for its artificial intelligence solution for climate-smart agriculture, against 11 finalist teams from Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda and Uganda. Its solar-powered AI cameras monitor crops in the field, detect pests and diseases early and send farmers SMS treatment recommendations in local languages, and the team will deploy the system over the next six months after a finalist bootcamp in Kigali, in a competition run with the FAO and Norad support.

stories.headline: Crankstart awards Morgan State University $800,000 to expand reentry scholarships for adult learners
stories.summary: Morgan State University's Center for Continuing and Professional Studies has received an $800,000 Crankstart Foundation grant to continue reentry scholarships for nontraditional adult learners pursuing their first bachelor's degrees. The four-year award, effective September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2030, extends a partnership running since 2016 that has brought Morgan nearly $2.4 million in scholarship support for returning students, in a state where about 600,000 working-age adults have college credits but no degree.

stories.headline: Wellcome Care Group Marks Successful Launch of Behavioral Health Platform for HBCU Students at AfroTech 2026
stories.summary: Wellcome Care Group has launched Wellcome, a digital behavioral health platform connecting HBCU students with licensed clinicians who understand their culture, identity and lived experience, debuting it at AfroTech Conference 2026 in Houston from November 3 to 6. Founded by Jack A. Brown, the platform offers virtual therapy, substance use counseling and care coordination, supported by Wellma, an AI navigation assistant, and began recruiting Black and Brown clinicians at the conference.

stories.headline: Meet Emma, The Black Woman AI Persona Raising Questions About Race, Identity, And Digital Blackface
stories.summary: Nuance Labs introduced Emma on November 9, a real-time AI persona presented as a Black woman who converses face to face using facial expressions, gestures and conversational cues, built over 18 months on the company's Nuplex 1.0 audiovisual model. AfroTech reports that Emma's face and voice were licensed from a real actress, but a team video does not visibly identify any Black team members, raising questions about representation, digital Blackface and who shapes AI identities.

stories.headline: After 340% Growth Without Outside Ownership, Mifland’s Founder Is Planning The Brand’s First Permanent Store In NYC
stories.summary: Nigerian-American designer Tobi Egberongbe has grown his independent fashion brand Mifland by 340 percent since the pandemic without giving up ownership, selling more than 200,000 products to over 61,000 customers, AfroTech reports. After sold-out pop-ups in New York and Atlanta and collaborations with Nike, the Atlanta Falcons and Sperry, the handcrafted leather goods label, worn organically by LeBron James and Jalen Hurts, is now planning its first permanent store in New York.

stories.headline: Kenya’s Satlyt Among 10 Startups Joining Google’s Applied AI Lab
stories.summary: Kenya's Satlyt, which recently raised $8 million for software that turns satellites into virtual AI data centers processing data in orbit, is among 10 startups chosen for Google's inaugural Africa Applied AI Lab, announced on November 11 from thousands of applications across more than 45 countries. The cohort, which also includes Nigeria's Intron, Termii and Vendy, Uganda's Crane AI Labs and Senegal's Tolbi, will work with Google engineers on Gemini and Gemma models ahead of a December demo day in Accra.

stories.headline: “Ghana’s money should buy Ghana’s rice”: Finance minister wants public kitchens tied to local farms by law
stories.summary: Ghana's Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson says the government will amend the Public Procurement Act so institutions spending public money on food must buy from Ghanaian farms, with locally grown rice at a minimum for schoolchildren and uniformed services. Forson told the Citi Breakfast Show on November 13 that the School Feeding Programme and Free Senior High School feeding together spend about GH¢6 billion a year, a market he wants local growers to be able to count on, with sanctions for institutions that ignore the rule.

stories.headline: More Employers, More Opportunities: Fall Career Fair Connects 766 Students With 89 Partners
stories.summary: Bowie State University's Fall 2026 Career and Internship Fair connected 766 students and alumni with recruiters from 89 organisations, including Enterprise Mobility, Motorola, Under Armour and WSSC, at the Martin Luther King, Jr. Center on November 4. Hosted by the Engage Center for Experiential Learning and Career Readiness, the fair is part of year-round support that includes resume help, interview preparation and one-on-one career appointments.

stories.headline: HBCU football league's gamble could have NCAA implications
stories.summary: The CIAA will make history on Friday night, November 13, when Fayetteville State and Virginia State meet in the inaugural Friday Night Blitz at Durham County Memorial Stadium, a third-versus-fourth-place game added to championship weekend with major NCAA Division II playoff implications. Both teams enter 7-3 overall and 6-2 in the CIAA, with Fayetteville State ranked seventh and Virginia State ninth in Super Region 1, from which eight teams reach the playoffs.

stories.headline: Lagos-based AI-powered entertainment company, Vibe Jungle Limited, secures $400,000
stories.summary: Lagos-based AI entertainment company Vibe Jungle Limited has reportedly secured $400,000 in founder-led investment, TechCabal reports. Founded in 2023 by chief executive Keziah Aboribo, the company offers a catalogue of pre-cleared music for independent artists and Nollywood productions and is developing an AI-powered platform for video generation and music production, currently in internal testing ahead of a public launch with subscription plans.

stories.headline: 8 Nigerian startups bag $4k each at FMYD, Cascador youth founders pitch day
stories.summary: Eight Nigerian startups have each won 5 million naira, about $4,000, in non-dilutive funding at the pitch day of the Founders Programme run by the Federal Ministry of Youth Development through the Nigerian Youth Academy and Cascador. The pilot drew more than 19,000 applications, with 17 founders from 13 states completing a four-week accelerator; the winners are SewPro, Biuda, Sparklean Station Nigeria, Backel Food Services, Shellify, Rekool Access Technology, Agrosavvy Consult and Craft Planet.

stories.headline: Billionaire Dangote raises Africa investment target to $70bn
stories.summary: Aliko Dangote, Africa's richest man, has raised his group's planned investment across the continent to $70 billion, $10 billion more than the $60 billion figure he gave on November 4, and says he is considering a 10,000-megawatt power programme that could include Nigeria. Dangote Industries has not said where the power plants would be built, how they would be financed or when they would start, and its announced projects across Africa already add up to more than $35 billion.

stories.headline: 2027 Budget: Government allocates GH¢389bn for spending, GH¢30bn for New Economy programme
stories.summary: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has presented Ghana's 2027 Budget to Parliament, a 389.2 billion cedi spending plan that introduces no new taxes and commits 30 billion cedis to the first year of a four-year, $10 billion New Economy Programme. The budget projects revenue and grants of 323.4 billion cedis, targets growth of at least 5.2 percent in 2027, and announces early redemption of 29 billion cedis in Domestic Debt Exchange Programme bonds due in February 2027.

stories.headline: Left-wing parties reject ANC coalition with DA, dismiss claims they would return if Ramaphosa resigns
stories.summary: South Africa's Conference of the Left, including the SACP, EFF, MK Party and Afrika Mayibuye Movement, has warned it will not support ANC-led coalitions with the DA in hung municipalities and has dismissed claims its parties would return to the ANC if President Cyril Ramaphosa resigns. Speaking in Boksburg on Thursday, the grouping, which says it secured just over 20 percent of the vote in the 2026 local elections, also called for the DA and Freedom Front Plus to be removed from the Government of National Unity.

stories.headline: Six people dead near Kenya's capital after building collapses - Citizen TV
stories.summary: Six people have died after the top floor of a building under construction collapsed on Friday in the Syokimau area southeast of Nairobi, Reuters reports, with five people taken to Imara Daima Hospital. Police disaster chief Duncan Ochieng said all 405 workers on site had been accounted for and the site was closed afterwards, in the latest of 24 building collapses recorded in Kenya in 2026 as of October, more than in any other year this decade.

stories.headline: ECOWAS appoints Akufo-Addo to lead Nigeria observer mission
stories.summary: Former Ghanaian President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo will lead 200 ECOWAS observers to monitor Nigeria's presidential and National Assembly elections on January 16, 2027, his office confirmed in a statement dated November 12. The delegation will bring together diplomats, election administrators and representatives of regional institutions and civil society, constituted under ECOWAS's 2001 Supplementary Protocol on Democracy and Good Governance.

stories.headline: Mudavadi, Mbadi Meet Kenyan Professionals in Ghana During AU Mission
stories.summary: Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi and Treasury Cabinet Secretary John Mbadi have met Kenyan professionals and businesspeople living in Ghana on Friday, November 13, on the sidelines of the 27th Extraordinary Session of the African Union Executive Council in Accra. The session focuses on sustainable financing of the African Union and its Peace Fund, with Kenya pushing reforms, championed by President William Ruto as AU Champion for Institutional Reform, to reduce the bloc's reliance on external funding.

stories.headline: Spartans Fall to No. 4 Duke at Echols Hall
stories.summary: No. 4 Duke scored the first 10 points and beat Norfolk State 85-23 on Thursday night in front of 1,982 fans at Joseph G. Echols Memorial Hall, becoming the first ACC program to play the Spartans at Echols Hall. Toby Fournier led Duke, now 3-0, with 20 points, while Alexis Davis led Norfolk State, now 1-3, with five points and six rebounds, and the Spartans next face Hampton in the Battle of the Bay on Saturday.

stories.headline: Pegula outlasts Noskova in 3 sets at WTA Finals, knocking out Gauff
stories.summary: Jessica Pegula saved a match point and won the final three games to beat Linda Noskova 7-6 (2), 4-6, 7-5 on Thursday night at Indian Wells and reach the WTA Finals semifinals, a result that knocked out Coco Gauff. Earlier, Gauff had rallied from 5-1 down in the second set to beat Marta Kostyuk 6-4, 7-5 despite serving problems and treatment for a stiff back, finishing Group 1 at 2-1 alongside Pegula and Noskova but missing the last four.

stories.headline: Hanifa Is Back: Anifa Mvuemba on 15 Years in Fashion, Rebuilding Her Brand and What Comes Next
stories.summary: Fifteen years after founding Hanifa, designer Anifa Mvuemba is relaunching the independent Black-owned luxury label with a new collection after stepping away from normal operations earlier this year amid public criticism and customer frustrations, following the birth of her second child. Mvuemba told EBONY the brand has added an external customer service team, new manufacturing partners, a third-party logistics provider and a direct purchase model, as she rebuilds the business around longevity and customer trust.

stories.headline: CAA And Ogilvy's New AI Platform Could Clone Celebrities To Create Advertisements
stories.summary: Creative Artists Agency and Ogilvy have launched ECHO, an AI advertising platform built on the CAA Vault, which captures, stores and licenses celebrities' likenesses, voices and intellectual property with their consent. AfroTech reports, citing The Hollywood Reporter, that the companies estimate ECHO could cut production costs by as much as 75 percent and turn a shoot producing eight to 10 assets into 30 to 50 pieces of content, with every advertisement requiring the featured celebrity's approval and carrying an AI watermark.

stories.headline: P-Valley Stars Nicco Annan and Shannon Thornton Headline HBCU First LOOK Film & TV Festival Presented by STARZ
stories.summary: The 4th Annual HBCU First LOOK Film & TV Festival, presented by STARZ, turned Howard University into a three-day masterclass from November 5 to 7 under the theme How to Be the Next, headlined by P-Valley stars Nicco Annan and Shannon Thornton. The festival's 2026 Film Challenge drew more than 450 submissions, with Florida A&M's Jada Davis winning the $5,000 grand prize for Rooted in Resilience: Black Farmer Perspectives on Land, Loss, and Legacy, and Howard's Mya Delgado and Coppin State's Christian Sutton also winning awards.

stories.headline: HBCU Chris-tal ball Week 11: two conference champs to be decided, but will there be a third?
stories.summary: Week 11 of the HBCU football season will crown the CIAA and SIAC champions on Saturday, November 14, with Virginia Union facing Johnson C. Smith in Durham and Kentucky State visiting Benedict, while North Carolina Central's visit to South Carolina State could effectively decide the MEAC race. HBCU Sports' predictions favour South Carolina State, Virginia Union and Benedict in those title contests, with Jackson State also tipped to win at Alabama State in the SWAC.

stories.headline: Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate race, breaking the GOP’s grip on the state
stories.summary: Democrat Scott Colom has defeated Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi, NBC News projects, flipping the reddest seat yet in this year's midterms and becoming Mississippi's first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction, in a state that last elected a Democrat to the Senate 44 years ago. Hyde-Smith conceded in a video message on Wednesday evening, Colom promised in Jackson to represent all Mississippians, and his victory means Democrats will hold at least 55 Senate seats in the next Congress.

stories.headline: ‘Not another dime’: Will Packer vows he’s done donating directly to FAMU, announces alumni-led fund free of ‘Florida politics’
stories.summary: Filmmaker and Florida A&M alumnus Will Packer has said he will no longer donate directly to the university, announcing in a social media video the formation of the Rattler Freedom Fund, an independent alumni fund intended to be free of Florida state politics. Packer cited the politically appointed trustees' appointment of President Marva B. Johnson and the board's approval of the largest compensation package in school history, pointed to a reported 35 percent drop in alumni donations, and called for radical transparency and independent financial power.

stories.headline: Claflin University’s UNCF Ecumenical Day of Prayer Breakfast Raises Nearly $50,000 for Student Scholarships
stories.summary: Claflin University's 2026 UNCF Ecumenical Day of Prayer brought together more than 300 guests and sponsors from the campus and surrounding Orangeburg communities and raised nearly $50,000 for the university's UNCF Scholarship Campaign, under the theme Investing in Minds & Transforming Futures. Pastor Dartanyan Jamerson presided over a program of prayer, music from the Claflin Gospel Choir D.R.E.A.M. and guest vocalist Minister Jason Singleton, and the funds will support scholarship opportunities for Claflin students.

stories.headline: Howard HBCU Center marks five years of advancing research, leadership and policy
stories.summary: Howard University's HBCU Center for Research, Leadership and Policy is marking its fifth year as a national hub for scholarship on America's 107 HBCUs, having funded 23 scholars, researchers and practitioners across areas from faculty mentorship to artificial intelligence. The center, conceptualized by Dr. Wayne A.I. Frederick and directed by Dr. Melanie Carter, also runs the Soul of the Yard podcast and the Turning Pages author series, and is inviting the public to the virtual launch of its Belonging At HBCUs toolkit.

stories.headline: Duke basketball makes historic trip to HBCU for women's game
stories.summary: No. 5 Duke visits Norfolk State on Thursday night, November 12, at Joseph G. Echols Memorial Hall, the Blue Devils' first road game at an HBCU since 1977 and the first visit by an ACC women's basketball program to Echols Hall. Duke arrives 2-0 under head coach Kara Lawson, while the Spartans, 1-2, have built a demanding nonconference schedule with six Power Four opponents as one of the MEAC's leading women's programs, with tipoff at 7 p.m. on the MEAC Network.

stories.headline: Faith and football: Alonzo Hampton’s belief has fueled a UAPB revival
stories.summary: Arkansas-Pine Bluff head coach Alonzo Hampton, a licensed minister who builds his program around daily devotionals and Bible study, has led the Golden Lions to a 6-3 overall and 4-2 SWAC record on a three-game winning streak after going 9-26 over his first three seasons. UAPB, ranked No. 6 in the latest Black College Football Poll, hosts reigning SWAC champion Prairie View A&M on Saturday at Simmons Bank Field in a game with major SWAC West implications.

stories.headline: Nigeria, Ghana, Senegal Headline African U-23 Olympic Qualifying Battles
stories.summary: Africa's U-23 heavyweights have begun the second qualifying round for the CAF U-23 Africa Cup of Nations Egypt 2027, which will decide the continent's representatives in men's football at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics, with 27 teams competing for 14 places in the final qualifying round. Nigeria's Olympic Eagles face DR Congo, first in Lubumbashi on November 13 and then in Ikenne on November 17, Ghana's Black Meteors open away to Libya in Benghazi, and Kenya, Senegal, Morocco, Cameroon and South Africa are also in action before return fixtures from November 15 to 17.

stories.headline: AFRICA-FX-Ghanaian and Zambian currencies under pressure
stories.summary: Traders expect Ghana's cedi and Zambia's kwacha to weaken against the dollar over the coming week, while the currencies of Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda are seen little changed, Reuters reports. The cedi traded at 11.70 to the dollar against 11.65 a week earlier on sustained corporate dollar demand, the kwacha was quoted at 20.74 against 20.62, Kenya's shilling held at 129.90/130.10 with central bank dollar sales, and Nigeria's naira was quoted at 1,348 on the official market, little changed from 1,346.

stories.headline: 11 Nigerian Startups Secure ₦300 Million at Wema Bank’s Hackaholics 7.0
stories.summary: Eleven Nigerian startups have secured a combined 300 million naira at the grand finale of Wema Bank's Hackaholics 7.0 in Lagos on November 6, from a competition that drew 5,329 participants and 1,632 ideas across seven pitch centres. The largest award, 60 million naira, went to Niteon's agritech platform connecting African farmers to processors, finance and international markets, with other winners spanning AI medical diagnostics, smart glasses for visually impaired people, plastic-waste building materials and women's healthcare.

stories.headline: Nigeria’s Raenest acquires UK-based payments company Remitise
stories.summary: Nigerian fintech Raenest has acquired UK-based payments company Remitise for an undisclosed amount, expanding its regulatory footprint and its control over its global payments infrastructure. Founded in 2022 by Victor Alade, Sodruldeen Mustapha and Richard Oyome, Raenest says it has more than one million individual customers in over 50 countries, has processed over $2 billion in payments and serves over 300 businesses, and the deal brings money services business and payment service provider licences in Canada alongside its Nigerian international money transfer operator licence.

stories.headline: Heritage Series Bank Notes Target Safer Business Transactions
stories.summary: President John Dramani Mahama has launched the Bank of Ghana's Heritage Series banknotes in Accra, an upgraded cedi series with reinforced cotton paper, enhanced security features and designs carrying Ghanaian historical figures, landmarks and cultural symbols, scheduled to enter circulation on December 1, 2026.
